grammarNote.en: We use the simple present to talk about things we usually or often do. Examples: I brush my teeth every day. On Saturdays, Dan sleeps late. I usually eat cereal for breakfast. Time words: every day, in the morning, once a week, usually, often, sometimes, on Sundays.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时用来描述经常做、习惯性做的事。例句：I brush my teeth every day.（我每天刷牙。）On Saturdays, Dan sleeps late.（星期六丹会睡懒觉。）常搭配的时间词：every day 每天、in the morning 早上、usually 通常、often 经常、sometimes 有时。

steps.en: Dan's alarm clock rings.
He wakes up.
He gets out of bed.
He goes into the bathroom.
He uses the toilet and flushes it.
He washes his hands.

notes.en: wake up = stop sleeping
notes.zh: wake up 意思是“停止睡眠、醒来”。

notes.en: wake up + get out of bed = get up. e.g. “What time did you get up?” “At 7:00.”
notes.zh: wake up（醒来）+ get out of bed（下床）合起来就是 get up（起床）。如问句 What time did you get up?（你几点起床的？）

notes.en: take a shower = wash yourself in a shower. You can also take a bath.
notes.zh: take a shower 是在淋浴下冲洗身体，也可以说 take a bath（泡澡）。

notes.en: Polite ways to say use the toilet: “go to the bathroom”, “use the bathroom”.
notes.zh: 想礼貌地表达“上厕所”，可以说 go to the bathroom 或 use the bathroom。

notes.en: When you flush a toilet, water cleans the toilet bowl.
notes.zh: 冲水（flush）时，水流会把马桶便池冲洗干净。

china.en: In China, many people wake up with a phone alarm instead of an alarm clock.
china.zh: 在中国，很多人用手机闹铃叫自己起床，而不是传统闹钟。可以说 set a phone alarm（定手机闹铃）。

china.en: “Wake up” (wake up) vs “get up” (get out of bed) is a very common pair in daily talk.
china.zh: wake up（醒来）和 get up（起床离床）是日常对话里非常常用的一对词，注意区分。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes habits, routines, and facts that are generally true. In this unit, Jenny follows her daily teeth-brushing routine. We often use time words like every day, usually, sometimes, and in the morning. Example: 'Jenny brushes her teeth every morning.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时用来描述习惯性动作、日常规律和客观事实。本单元中珍妮每天重复同样的刷牙流程。常用时间词有 every day（每天）、usually（通常）、sometimes（有时）、in the morning（早上）。例句：Jenny brushes her teeth every morning.（珍妮每天早上刷牙。）

steps.en: Jenny runs some water over her toothbrush.
She squeezes toothpaste onto her toothbrush.
She moves her toothbrush up and down and back and forth.
steps.zh: 她把牙刷上下、来回地刷。

steps.en: To rinse her mouth, she takes some water and swishes it back and forth in her mouth.
steps.zh: 为了漱口，她含了一口水，在嘴里来回漱。

steps.en: Then she spits it into the sink.
steps.zh: 然后她把水吐进水池里。

steps.en: She rinses off her toothbrush.
Then she puts it back in the toothbrush rack.
steps.zh: 然后把牙刷放回牙刷架上。

steps.en: She flosses her teeth by pulling out a long piece of floss.
steps.zh: 她用牙线洁牙：先抽出一段长长的牙线。

steps.en: She slips it between her teeth.
She moves it back and forth and up and down.
steps.zh: 然后前后、上下地移动牙线。

notes.en: You run water over something by using water from a faucet or pipe and letting the water flow away after hitting the thing.
notes.zh: run water over something 指打开水龙头或水管，让水冲过物体表面后流走。

notes.en: Something goes back and forth by going from one side to another (left and right) many times.
notes.zh: back and forth 指从一边到另一边来回多次（左右方向）。

notes.en: Something goes up and down by going in these directions (up and down) many times.
notes.zh: up and down 指在上下方向来回多次。

notes.en: You slip something somewhere by moving it gently into a small space.
notes.zh: slip something somewhere 指轻轻地把某物塞进狭小的空间。

china.en: Many Chinese families store toothbrushes upright in a rinsing cup, not on a wall-mounted rack.
china.zh: 中国家庭常把牙刷头朝上放在漱口杯里，而不是挂在壁挂牙刷架上。

china.en: Many people in China use a cup to hold water for brushing, rather than running water directly from the faucet.
china.zh: 很多中国人刷牙时用杯子接水，而不是直接对着水龙头冲。

china.en: Electric toothbrushes and water flossers are becoming common in Chinese cities.
china.zh: 电动牙刷和冲牙器在中国城市家庭中越来越常见。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes habits and routines. In this unit, Dan goes through his daily shower routine. Time markers like every morning, usually, and after that often appear. Example: 'Dan takes a shower every morning.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时用于描述习惯和日常流程。本单元中丹每天重复同样的淋浴步骤。常见时间标志词有 every morning（每天早上）、usually（通常）、after that（之后）。例句：Dan takes a shower every morning.（丹每天早上淋浴。）

steps.en: Dan pulls the shower curtain shut.
By turning the knob, he turns the water on.
steps.zh: 他转动旋钮，打开水龙头。

steps.en: He washes his hair with shampoo and the rest of his body with soap.
steps.zh: 他用洗发水洗头，用香皂洗身体其他部位。

steps.en: Then he rinses off with water.
steps.zh: 然后他用水把身上冲干净。

steps.en: After turning the water off, he steps out of the shower.
steps.zh: 关掉水之后，他走出淋浴间。

steps.en: He takes a towel from the towel rack.
steps.zh: 他从毛巾架上取下毛巾。

steps.en: Then he dries himself off.
He wraps a towel around himself and dries his hair.
steps.zh: 他把毛巾裹在身上，擦干头发。

steps.en: He puts some deodorant under his arms.
steps.zh: 他在腋下抹一些除臭剂。

notes.en: Use 'dry off' only if the water stays on top of the thing that is wet. You don't 'dry off' your hair or a towel. You 'dry' them or 'dry them out.'
notes.zh: dry off 只用于物体表面有水的情况。不要说 dry off your hair 或 dry off a towel，而要说 dry them 或 dry them out。

notes.en: Pull something shut = pull it until it is shut.
notes.zh: pull something shut 指把某物拉到关上为止。

notes.en: Take some students out of your classroom. The others (those still in the room) are the rest of the class.
notes.zh: 把一部分学生带出教室，剩下的（仍在教室里的）就是 the rest of the class（班上其余的人）。

notes.en: After you turn something on, it runs or works. After you turn it off, it stops.
notes.zh: turn on 之后某物开始运转；turn off 之后它就停止。

notes.en: A deodorant is something that takes away bad smells.
notes.zh: deodorant（除臭剂）是用来去除异味的东西。

china.en: Chinese bathrooms usually have a glass shower screen or wet-dry separation, not a cloth shower curtain.
china.zh: 中国浴室常用玻璃隔断做干湿分离，而不是布浴帘。

china.en: Most Chinese homes use a gas or electric water heater; the shower head is often hand-held.
china.zh: 中国家庭多用燃气或电热水器，淋浴喷头多为手持花洒。

china.en: Deodorant is less common in China; many people use antiperspirant roll-ons or perfume instead.
china.zh: 除臭剂在中国不太普及，很多人用止汗走珠或香水代替。

grammarNote.en: The simple present is used for repeated daily actions. In this unit, Tom puts on his clothes step by step every morning. Notice word order: 'Tom puts on his underwear' = 'Tom puts his underwear on.' With it/them, 'on' moves away from 'put.' Example: 'Tom picks up his shirt and puts it on.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时用于每天重复的动作。本单元中汤姆每天早上一步步穿衣服。注意语序：put on 可分开说 put on his underwear = put his underwear on；当代词 it/them 作宾语时，on 要放到代词后面，如 puts it on（穿上它）。例句：Tom picks up his shirt and puts it on.（汤姆拿起衬衫穿上。）

steps.en: Tom puts on some underwear, a T-shirt, some socks, some pants, and a shirt.
steps.zh: 汤姆穿上内裤、T恤、袜子、裤子和衬衫。

steps.en: Tom steps into his pants and then pulls them up.
steps.zh: 汤姆把腿伸进裤子里，然后把裤子提上来。

steps.en: He fastens the waistband and zips up the fly.
He slips a belt through the belt loops and buckles it.
steps.zh: 他把皮带穿过皮带袢，然后扣好。

steps.en: Tom slips an arm into each sleeve.
steps.zh: 汤姆把两只胳膊分别伸进袖子里。

steps.en: He buttons the shirt and the cuffs.
steps.zh: 他扣上衬衫的扣子和袖口的扣子。

steps.en: He straightens his collar.
He tucks his shirt into his pants.
steps.zh: 他把衬衫下摆塞进裤子里。

notes.en: Usually 'a pair of something' means 2. 'A pair of cats' means '2 cats.'
notes.zh: 通常 a pair of 表示“两个”。a pair of cats 就是“两只猫”。

notes.en: But some items of clothing are called a pair even though they seem like 1 thing: 'a pair of pants.'
notes.zh: 但有些衣物虽然看起来是一件，却用 a pair 来表示，例如 a pair of pants（一条裤子）。

notes.en: You can say 'a sock' or 'a shoe,' but when talking about clothes, do NOT say 'a pant,' 'a pajama,' 'an underpant,' 'a short,' or 'a glass.'
notes.zh: 你可以说 a sock、a shoe，但谈论衣物时不能说 a pant、a pajama、an underpant、a short 或 a glass。

notes.en: 'Tom puts on his underwear' = 'Tom puts his underwear on.' These mean the same. With it or them, 'on' moves away from 'put.'
notes.zh: Tom puts on his underwear 与 Tom puts his underwear on 意思相同。当代词 it/them 作宾语时，on 要放到代词后面，如 puts it on。

china.en: Chinese men usually wear casual or business-casual clothes for work; formal Western suits are less common than in the US.
china.zh: 中国男性上班多穿休闲或商务休闲装，正式西装比美国少见。

china.en: Traditional Chinese clothing like the Tang jacket uses frog buttons (pankou) instead of zippers and buckles.
china.zh: 中式服装如唐装使用盘扣，而不是拉链和皮带扣。

china.en: Most Chinese men wear socks with leather shoes; sandals without socks are less common in formal settings.
china.zh: 中国男性穿皮鞋时通常会穿袜子，凉鞋不穿袜子在正式场合较少见。

grammarNote.en: The simple present is used here to describe what Pam wears depending on the weather. Note weather expressions: 'It's hot/cold.' 'It's raining/snowing.' Example: 'If it's hot, Pam wears light clothes.'
grammarNote.zh: 本单元用一般现在时描述帕姆根据天气穿衣的习惯。注意天气表达：It's hot/cold.（天热/冷。）It's raining/snowing.（下雨/下雪。）例句：If it's hot, Pam wears light clothes.（天热时，帕姆穿轻薄衣服。）

steps.en: Pam puts on some panties, a bra, and a dress, or a blouse and a skirt, or some pants.
steps.zh: 帕姆穿上内裤、文胸，再穿连衣裙，或女式衬衫配短裙，或裤子。

steps.en: She puts on some socks, or some nylons (stockings), or some pantyhose.
steps.zh: 她穿上袜子，或尼龙长袜，或连裤袜。

steps.en: If it's hot, Pam wears light clothes: a short-sleeved cotton shirt and a pair of cotton shorts.
steps.zh: 天热时，帕姆穿轻薄衣服：短袖棉质衬衫和一条棉短裤。

steps.en: She goes barefoot indoors and wears sandals outdoors.
steps.zh: 她在家里光脚，出门时穿凉鞋。

steps.en: Dressing this way keeps her cool.
If it's cold, Pam wears heavy clothes: a long-sleeved shirt, a wool sweater, and long pants.
steps.zh: 天冷时，帕姆穿厚衣服：长袖衬衫、羊毛毛衣和长裤。

steps.en: She wears thick wool socks.
Before going outdoors, she puts on a heavy coat and some gloves or mittens.
steps.zh: 出门前，她穿上厚外套，戴上手套或连指手套。

steps.en: She wraps a scarf around her neck, puts on a hat, and wears some boots.
steps.zh: 她把围巾围在脖子上，戴上帽子，穿上靴子。

steps.en: Dressing this way keeps her warm.

notes.en: Someone who goes barefoot walks around with no shoes or socks on his/her feet. His/Her feet are bare.
notes.zh: go barefoot 指脚上不穿鞋也不穿袜子，光脚走路。

notes.en: If something keeps her cool, it helps her stay cool.
notes.zh: keep her cool 指帮助她保持凉爽。

notes.en: Some ways to talk about the weather: 1. Use it + BE + an adjective: It's hot. It's hot outside. 2. Use it + BE + the -ing form of a weather verb: It's raining. It's snowing.
notes.zh: 谈论天气的几种方式：1. 用 it + BE + 形容词：It's hot. / It's hot outside. 2. 用 it + BE + 天气动词的 -ing 形式：It's raining. / It's snowing.

notes.en: After you put on your clothes, you wear them.
notes.zh: put on 是“穿上”的动作，wear 是“穿着”的状态。

notes.en: COTTON: a fabric that comes from the cotton plant.
notes.zh: COTTON（棉）：一种来自棉花植物的面料。

notes.en: WOOL: a fabric that comes from a sheep.
notes.zh: WOOL（羊毛）：一种来自绵羊的面料。

notes.en: If something is outside a building, it is outdoors. If something is inside a building, it is indoors.
notes.zh: outdoors 指在建筑物外面；indoors 指在建筑物里面。

china.en: Chinese women often wear pants or skirts to work; pantyhose/stockings are more common in winter.
china.zh: 中国女性上班多穿裤装或裙装，连裤袜/长袜在冬季更常见。

china.en: Homes in northern China have central heating in winter, so people take off heavy coats indoors.
china.zh: 中国北方冬季室内有暖气，进屋后常脱掉厚外套。

china.en: The cheongsam (qipao) is a traditional Chinese dress with frog buttons and often made of silk.
china.zh: 旗袍是中国传统女装，使用盘扣，面料常为丝绸。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes a routine task done every morning. Notice the sequence words: first, then, next. Example: 'I put a bottom sheet on the mattress. Then I tuck the top sheet under the mattress.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述每天早上重复的铺床流程。注意顺序词 first（首先）、then（然后）、next（接着）。例句：I put a bottom sheet on the mattress. Then I tuck the top sheet under the mattress.（我把床单铺在床垫上，然后把上端的床单塞到床垫下面。）

steps.en: I put a bottom sheet on the mattress. If I have a fitted sheet, I slip it over the mattress.
steps.zh: 我把床单铺在床垫上。如果是松紧床笠，我把它套在床垫上。

steps.en: If I have a flat sheet, I tuck it under the mattress.
steps.zh: 如果是普通床单，我把它塞到床垫下面。

steps.en: Then I tuck the top sheet under the mattress at the foot of the bed.
steps.zh: 然后我把上端的床单在床尾塞到床垫下面。

steps.en: I pull the top sheet tight.
I spread a blanket over the bed and smooth it out.
steps.zh: 我在床上铺一条毯子，然后抹平。

steps.en: I spread a bedspread over the bed.
I fluff up the pillows and lay them at the head of the bed.
steps.zh: 我把枕头拍松，放在床头。

steps.en: I pull the bedspread over the pillows and smooth it out.
steps.zh: 我把床罩拉过枕头，然后抹平。

notes.en: To pull something tight is to pull it until it is tight.
notes.zh: pull something tight 指把某物拉到绷紧为止。

notes.en: When you lie on a bed, you put your head near the head of the bed and your feet near the foot of the bed.
notes.zh: 躺在床上时，头靠近床头（head of the bed），脚靠近床尾（foot of the bed）。

notes.en: A pillow goes inside a pillowcase.
notes.zh: 枕头（pillow）装在枕套（pillowcase）里面。

notes.en: The corners of a fitted sheet are made to fit over the corners of a mattress. Fitted sheets are used only as bottom sheets, not as top sheets.
notes.zh: 松紧床笠的四角是为套住床垫四角设计的。床笠只能当床单（bottom sheet）用，不能当盖单（top sheet）用。

notes.en: You smooth out a sheet by removing wrinkles.
notes.zh: smooth out 指把褶皱抹平。

china.en: Many Chinese simply fold the quilt into a rectangle or square in the morning instead of making a layered bed.
china.zh: 很多中国人早上把被子叠成方块或对折即可，不一定要铺床罩。

china.en: Chinese bedding often uses a duvet cover (beitao) instead of a top sheet plus blanket plus bedspread.
china.zh: 中国床品常用被套，而不是床单+毯子+床罩三层。

china.en: Hotel-style bed making with a bedspread is common in star hotels, but less so in ordinary homes.
china.zh: 带床罩的酒店式铺法在星级酒店常见，普通家庭较少。

grammarNote.en: The simple present is used to describe a repeated routine (making coffee or tea every morning). Watch the cause-and-effect chain: water heats up → drips through coffee → becomes coffee. Example: 'Pam scoops ground coffee into the filter.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述每天早上冲咖啡/泡茶的重复流程。注意因果链：水加热→滴过咖啡粉→变成咖啡。例句：Pam scoops ground coffee into the filter.（帕姆把磨好的咖啡舀进滤篮。）

steps.en: Pam scoops some ground coffee into the filter.
steps.zh: 帕姆把磨好的咖啡舀进滤篮。

steps.en: Then she pours some water into the coffee maker.
steps.zh: 然后她把水倒进咖啡机。

steps.en: She turns the coffee maker on by pressing the switch.
steps.zh: 她按下开关启动咖啡机。

steps.en: The water heats up and drips through the ground coffee into the coffeepot.
steps.zh: 水加热后滴过咖啡粉，滴进咖啡壶里。

steps.en: Dan boils water in a teakettle.
He pours the hot water into a teapot and adds some tea leaves.
steps.zh: 他把热水倒进茶壶，加入一些茶叶。

steps.en: As the tea leaves soak in the water, the water becomes tea.
steps.zh: 茶叶泡在水里时，水就变成了茶。

steps.en: Dan strains the tea.
Then he adds sugar and milk, and stirs his tea.
steps.zh: 然后他加糖和牛奶，搅拌茶水。

notes.en: A filter has very small holes in it. A liquid or gas can pass through the holes, but large pieces of a solid cannot. A strainer does the same thing, but its holes are larger and it probably has a handle.
notes.zh: filter（滤纸/滤篮）上有非常小的孔，液体或气体能通过，但大颗粒固体不行。strainer（滤器）作用相同，但孔更大，通常有手柄。

notes.en: If you grind coffee beans, you get ground coffee.
notes.zh: 把咖啡豆磨碎，就得到 ground coffee（咖啡粉）。

notes.en: Scoop...coffee = move it by using a scoop.
notes.zh: scoop...coffee 指用勺子把咖啡舀起来。

notes.en: Heats up = becomes hot.
notes.zh: heat up 意思是“变热”。

notes.en: When something soaks, it stays in water and becomes very wet.
notes.zh: soak 指某物泡在水里，变得很湿。

china.en: Chinese people usually drink hot tea in the morning, often steeping tea leaves directly in a glass or mug rather than using a teapot.
china.zh: 中国人早上多喝热茶，常用玻璃杯或马克杯直接泡茶，而不是用 teapot。

china.en: Coffee is popular in cities, but many people drink instant coffee or use capsule/pod machines rather than drip coffee makers.
china.zh: 咖啡在中国城市很流行，但很多人喝速溶咖啡或用胶囊机，而不是滴漏式咖啡机。

china.en: Gongfu tea uses a small clay teapot and tiny cups, without milk or sugar.
china.zh: 功夫茶用小紫砂壶和小茶杯，不加奶也不加糖。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes the morning routine of preparing breakfast. Note the opposite pairs: lower/raise, pop up. Example: 'Dan puts two slices of bread into the toaster. The toast pops up when it's done.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述准备早餐的晨间流程。注意反义词组：lower（放下）/ raise（举起）、pop up（弹起）。例句：Dan puts two slices of bread into the toaster. The toast pops up when it's done.（丹把两片面包放进烤面包机，吐司烤好时会弹起来。）

steps.en: Pam pours some cereal from the box into her bowl.
steps.zh: 帕姆把麦片从盒子里倒进碗里。

steps.en: She pours in some milk and sprinkles some sugar on her cereal.
steps.zh: 她倒入一些牛奶，在麦片上撒一些糖。

steps.en: Then she peels a banana, slices it, and puts the slices on her cereal.
steps.zh: 然后她剥一根香蕉，切片，放在麦片上。

steps.en: Dan puts two slices of bread into the toaster.
steps.zh: 丹把两片面包放进烤面包机。

steps.en: By pressing the starter, he lowers the bread into the toaster.
steps.zh: 按下启动杆，他把面包降进烤面包机里。

steps.en: Hot wires inside the toaster toast the bread.
steps.zh: 烤面包机里的电热丝把面包烤成吐司。

steps.en: The toast pops up when it's done.
Dan spreads some butter and jam on his toast.
steps.zh: 丹在吐司上涂一些黄油和果酱。

notes.en: You sprinkle something by making small pieces of it fall over a wide area.
notes.zh: sprinkle 指把细小的东西均匀地撒在一大片区域上。

notes.en: Something that pops up comes up very quickly.
notes.zh: pop up 指非常快速地弹起来。

notes.en: When you make something go down, you lower it; when you make something go up, you raise it.
notes.zh: 让某物下去叫 lower，让某物上去叫 raise。

notes.en: When you peel a fruit or vegetable, you take off its skin. Afterwards, the skin that has been taken off is called 'a peel' or 'peelings.'
notes.zh: peel 指削掉水果或蔬菜的皮；削下来的皮叫 peel 或 peelings。

notes.en: Slices of bread are also called 'pieces' of bread.
notes.zh: 面包的片也可以叫 pieces of bread。

notes.en: To slice something is to cut it into thin, flat pieces.
notes.zh: slice 指把某物切成薄而平的片。

china.en: Cold cereal with milk is uncommon in China; Chinese breakfast is usually hot porridge, soy milk, steamed buns, or fried dough sticks.
china.zh: 冷麦片加牛奶在中国不常见；中式早餐多为热粥、豆浆、包子、油条。

china.en: Toasters are not common in Chinese homes; people heat mantou (steamed buns) or bread in a pan or oven.
china.zh: 烤面包机在中国家庭不普及，人们用平底锅或烤箱加热馒头片或面包。

china.en: Chinese toast is often spread with condensed milk, bean paste, or rou sauce instead of butter and jam.
china.zh: 中式吐司常抹炼乳、豆沙或肉酱，而不是黄油和果酱。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes a repeated cooking routine. Notice that both active and middle forms work: 'Dan fries the egg' = 'The egg fries.' Example: 'He cracks an egg into the pan. The egg fries.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述每天重复的烹饪流程。注意主动与中性形式都可用：Dan fries the egg.（丹煎鸡蛋。）= The egg fries.（鸡蛋在煎。）例句：He cracks an egg into the pan. The egg fries.（他把鸡蛋磕进锅里，鸡蛋煎着。）

steps.en: There are four burners on Dan's stove.
steps.zh: 丹的炉子上有四个炉头。

steps.en: He turns on the gas, and one of the burners lights.
steps.zh: 他打开煤气，其中一个炉头点燃了。

steps.en: He puts a frying pan on the burner and melts some butter in the pan.
steps.zh: 他把煎锅放在炉头上，在锅里融化一些黄油。

steps.en: He cracks an egg into the pan and throws the shell into the garbage.
steps.zh: 他把一个鸡蛋磕进锅里，把蛋壳扔进垃圾桶。

steps.en: The egg fries.
Dan flips it over once with a spatula and then takes it out of the pan.
steps.zh: 丹用锅铲把它翻一次，然后把它从锅里盛出来。

steps.en: He puts the egg on a plate.

notes.en: 'The egg fries' and 'Dan fries the egg' are both possible.
notes.zh: The egg fries. 和 Dan fries the egg. 两种说法都可以。

notes.en: Dan has a gas stove. Some people have electric stoves.
notes.zh: 丹用燃气灶，有些人用电炉。

notes.en: When you flip something, you turn it upside down.
notes.zh: flip 指把某物上下翻转。

notes.en: When you throw something into the garbage, you throw it into a container for garbage.
notes.zh: throw into the garbage 指扔进装垃圾的容器里。

notes.en: To melt something is to heat it until it changes from solid to liquid.
notes.zh: melt 指加热某物，使其从固体变成液体。

china.en: Chinese people usually fry eggs in an iron wok or frying pan with more oil, often making a 'fried egg with a crispy edge' (jidan).
china.zh: 中国人常用铁锅或平底锅煎蛋，油较多，常煎成边缘酥脆的荷包蛋。

china.en: Most Chinese kitchens use a gas stove or induction cooktop; four-burner ranges and ovens are less common.
china.zh: 中国厨房多用燃气灶或电磁炉，四眼灶和烤箱较少见。

china.en: A Chinese fried egg is often eaten with congee, fried dough sticks, or soy milk, not with bacon and toast.
china.zh: 中式煎蛋常配粥、油条、豆浆，而不是培根和吐司。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes the ongoing breakfast routine. Note frequency adverbs like 'sometimes' and the phrase 'a little bit.' Example: 'Pam and Dan sit down at the table. Sometimes, he dips his toast into the yolk.'
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述吃早餐时的日常状态。注意频率副词 sometimes（有时）和短语 a little bit（一点点）。例句：Pam and Dan sit down at the table. Sometimes, he dips his toast into the yolk.（帕姆和丹在餐桌旁坐下。有时他把吐司蘸进蛋黄里。）

steps.en: Pam and Dan sit down at the table.
steps.zh: 帕姆和丹在餐桌旁坐下。

steps.en: Pam drinks some coffee from her mug and eats some cereal.
steps.zh: 帕姆用马克杯喝咖啡，吃一些麦片。

steps.en: Dan drinks some tea and has an egg with bacon and toast.
steps.zh: 丹喝茶，吃一个鸡蛋配培根和吐司。

steps.en: Sometimes, he dips his toast into the yolk of his egg.
steps.zh: 有时他把吐司蘸进蛋黄里。

steps.en: As they eat, they read the paper and talk a little bit.
steps.zh: 他们一边吃一边看报纸，聊几句。

steps.en: After eating, they wipe their lips with their napkins and leave the table.
steps.zh: 吃完后，他们用餐巾擦嘴，然后离开餐桌。

notes.en: 'The paper' means 'the newspaper.'
notes.zh: the paper 指 the newspaper（报纸）。

notes.en: A little bit = some, but not very much.
notes.zh: a little bit 意思是“一点点”，即有一些但不多。

notes.en: First you sit down; then you sit.
notes.zh: sit down 是“坐下”的动作，sit 是“坐着”的状态。

notes.en: A mug is a large cup with a handle.
notes.zh: mug 指带把手的大杯子。

notes.en: Pam and Dan sit at the table. They sit in or on chairs.
notes.zh: sit at the table 指坐在桌边；sit in/on chairs 指坐在椅子上。

notes.en: You dip a solid into a liquid by putting it in for only a short time.
notes.zh: dip 指把固体短暂地浸入液体中。

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: It says here that taxes are going up.

china.en: Many Chinese people read news or watch short videos on their phones while eating breakfast, rather than reading a newspaper.
china.zh: 很多中国人吃早餐时用手机看新闻或刷短视频，而不是读报纸。

china.en: Chinese breakfast uses chopsticks and bowls; knives and forks are rarely used at home.
china.zh: 中式早餐用筷子和碗，家里很少用刀叉。

china.en: Many Chinese eat breakfast at a street-side stall (soymilk, steamed buns) rather than sitting at a dining table at home.
china.zh: 很多中国人在路边摊吃早餐（豆浆、包子），而不是坐在家里餐桌旁。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes the final steps of the morning routine. Example: 'Tom puts on a jacket and zips it up. He picks up his keys and wallet.' Notice the phrasal verbs: zip up, pick up, put in, say goodbye.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述晨间流程的最后几步。例句：Tom puts on a jacket and zips it up. He picks up his keys and wallet.（汤姆穿上外套，拉上拉链。他拿起钥匙和钱包。）注意短语动词：zip up（拉上拉链）、pick up（拿起）、put in（放进）、say goodbye（道别）。

steps.en: Tom puts on a jacket and zips it up.
steps.zh: 汤姆穿上外套，拉上拉链。

steps.en: He puts on his shoes and ties them.
He picks up his keys and wallet and puts them in his pockets.
steps.zh: 他拿起钥匙和钱包，放进兜里。

steps.en: He picks up his backpack.
Then he says goodbye to Jenny.
He opens the door, steps outside, and shuts the door.
steps.zh: 他打开门，走到门外，然后关上门。

notes.en: Some ways people say goodbye: 'See you later.' 'Bye.' 'See you.' 'Catch you later.' 'Goodbye.'
notes.zh: 道别的几种说法：See you later. / Bye. / See you. / Catch you later. / Goodbye.

notes.en: 'Leave home' can mean the same as 'leave the house.' (For example, 'He left home at seven o'clock this morning.')
notes.zh: leave home 与 leave the house 意思相同。例如：He left home at seven o'clock this morning.（他今天早上七点出门。）

notes.en: The opposite of 'zip up' is 'unzip.'
notes.zh: zip up 的反义词是 unzip（拉开拉链）。

notes.en: 'Shut the door' means 'close the door.'
notes.zh: shut the door 意思就是 close the door（关门）。

china.en: Many Chinese leave home with a phone instead of a wallet, paying by scanning QR codes; keys are often replaced by access cards or phone Bluetooth.
china.zh: 很多中国人出门带手机而不是钱包，扫码支付；钥匙常被门禁卡或手机蓝牙代替。

china.en: Chinese farewell phrases include 'zàijiàn' (goodbye), 'lù shàng xiǎo xīn' (take care on the road), and 'màn zǒu' (take care).
china.zh: 中国人道别常说“再见”“路上小心”“慢走”。

china.en: Urban commuters in China usually take the subway or bus with a backpack or commuter bag, rather than driving.
china.zh: 中国城市通勤族多背双肩包或通勤包，乘地铁/公交上班，而不是开车。

grammarNote.en: "Getting Around" uses mostly simple past verbs. Regular verbs end in -ed (e.g., walked, checked, waited). Irregular verbs have special past forms, listed in brackets in Key Vocabulary (e.g., sit-sat, stand-stood, get-got, hold-held, pay-paid, put-put, read-read, ride-rode, ring-rang). Common past-tense time expressions include: Yesterday; phrases with "last" (last week, last year, last month, last Monday); phrases with "ago" (two weeks ago, a few minutes ago, five days ago, a year ago).
grammarNote.zh: 本单元主要使用一般过去时。规则动词过去式加 -ed（如 walked、checked、waited）。不规则动词有特殊的过去式，列在"核心词汇"括号内（如 sit-sat、stand-stood、get-got、hold-held、pay-paid、put-put、read-read、ride-rode、ring-rang）。与过去时连用的常见时间词包括：Yesterday（昨天）；带 last 的短语（last week 上周、last year 去年、last month 上个月、last Monday 上周一）；带 ago 的短语（two weeks ago 两周前、a few minutes ago 几分钟前、five days ago 五天前、a year ago 一年前）。

steps.en: Jenny checked her bus schedule.
steps.zh: Jenny 查看了她的公交时刻表。

steps.en: Her bus—a Number 77—was due at eight-twenty.
steps.zh: 她要乘坐的 77 路公交车预计八点二十到。

steps.en: She walked to the bus stop...
...and sat on a bench to wait for the bus.
The bus arrived on time (at eight-twenty).
steps.zh: 公交车准点到达（八点二十）。

steps.en: The driver opened the door...
...and Jenny got on the bus.
She showed the driver her bus pass.
steps.zh: 她向司机出示了公交卡。

steps.en: Other passengers paid their fare.
All the seats were full, so Jenny stood in the aisle.
steps.zh: 所有座位都满了，所以 Jenny 站在过道里。

steps.en: She held on to a strap on the overhead bars.
steps.zh: 她抓着头顶横杆上的吊环。

steps.en: Soon, someone got off the bus, so a seat was empty.
steps.zh: 不久有人下车，空出了一个座位。

steps.en: Jenny sat down and read a book while she rode the bus.
steps.zh: Jenny 坐下来，边坐车边看书。

steps.en: Near her stop, she pressed a button...
steps.zh: 快到站时，她按了一下按钮……

steps.en: ...to ring the "stop" signal.
She walked to the exit...
...and got off at her stop.
steps.zh: 然后在自己那站下了车。

notes.en: If a bus is NOT on time, it is late or early.
notes.zh: 如果公交车不准时，就是晚点或早点了。

notes.en: If Jenny checked her schedule, she looked at it for a short time to find some specific information.
notes.zh: Jenny 查看时刻表，意思是她短暂地看一下，找出特定信息。

notes.en: A bus pass is a card or a piece of paper.
notes.zh: 公交卡是一张卡片或一张纸。

notes.en: A bus pass means you can ride the bus without paying on the bus.
notes.zh: 有了公交卡，坐车时就不用再当场付钱。

notes.en: A bus pass is good for a certain time (maybe one week, maybe one month, etc.).
notes.zh: 公交卡在一段时间内有效（可能一周、一个月等）。

china.en: In Chinese cities, most people pay bus fare by scanning a QR code with their phone or by tapping a transit card, instead of dropping coins into a fare box.
china.zh: 在中国城市，大多数人用手机扫码或刷交通卡付公交费，而不是往投币箱里塞硬币。

china.en: Many Chinese buses have air conditioning and automatic next-stop announcements in Mandarin and English.
china.zh: 中国很多公交车有空调，并用普通话和英语自动报站。

china.en: Contactless transit cards (like Beijing's Yikatong) and shared-bike apps are widely used for short trips.
china.zh: 短途出行广泛使用非接触式交通卡（如北京一卡通）和共享单车 App。

grammarNote.en: We use the simple past to tell what happened at a specific time in the past. Regular verbs add -ed (start → started); irregular verbs change (sit → sat, put → put). Time words: yesterday, this morning, last week, at 7:00.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时用来叙述过去某个时间发生的事。规则动词加 -ed（start → started）；不规则动词有特殊变化（sit → sat 坐，put → put 放）。常用时间词：yesterday 昨天、this morning 今天早上、last week 上周。

steps.en: Kate sat in the driver's seat, and her friends sat in the passenger seats.
steps.zh: 凯特坐在驾驶座上，朋友们坐在乘客座位上。

steps.en: She adjusted her seat and the rear-view mirror.
steps.zh: 她调整了座椅和后视镜。

steps.en: She buckled her seat belt.
Kate put the key into the ignition.
steps.zh: 凯特把钥匙插入点火开关。

steps.en: She turned the key.
She started the car.
She looked over her shoulder.
steps.zh: 她回头看了看（肩膀后方）。

steps.en: She backed out of the driveway.

notes.en: adjust = move or change something until it is right for you.
notes.zh: adjust 指“调整”，把某物移动或改变到合适的状态。

notes.en: A driveway is the short road that leads from the street to a house or a parking lot.
notes.zh: driveway 是连接街道与房屋或停车场的短车道。

notes.en: The ignition is the slot where you put the car key. In other cases, “ignition” means starting to burn.
notes.zh: ignition 是插入车钥匙的孔（点火开关）；在别的语境里也可以指“点燃、起火”。

china.en: In China, before starting out you also adjust the seat and mirrors, and you must wear a seat belt.
china.zh: 在中国开车前同样要先调座椅和后视镜，并且全车人员都必须系安全带。

china.en: Many cars in China are automatic (自动挡), so people just put it in D, release the brake, and go.
china.zh: 中国很多车是自动挡，挂 D 挡、松刹车就能起步；手动挡（manual）则需要踩离合挂挡。

china.en: Before backing up, Chinese drivers also check the rear-view mirror and the blind spot.
china.zh: 倒车前，中国司机同样要看后视镜和盲区（blind spot），确认安全。

grammarNote.en: The simple past describes completed actions in the past. Regular verbs add -ed (e.g., stepped, pressed, turned). Irregular verbs in this unit include: let-let, put-put, take-took. Time expressions like when it got dark, when it rained, and as the car speeded up set the past scene.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时描述过去完成的动作。规则动词加 -ed（如 stepped、pressed、turned）。本单元的不规则动词有：let-let、put-put、take-took。时间表达如 when it got dark（天黑时）、when it rained（下雨时）、as the car speeded up（汽车加速时）都用来设定过去的场景。

steps.en: Kate stepped on the clutch pedal,...
...shifted into gear,...
...and took her foot off the clutch.
To go faster, Kate pressed the accelerator.
steps.zh: 为了加速，Kate 踩下油门。

steps.en: As the car speeded up,...
...she shifted into a higher gear.
To slow down, Kate let up on the accelerator...
steps.zh: 为了减速，Kate 松开油门……

steps.en: ...and shifted into a lower gear.
steps.zh: 然后换入了更低的挡位。

steps.en: The car slowed down.
Kate stepped on the brake.
Kate put her turn signal on...
...and turned the steering wheel.
When it got dark, she turned on the lights.
When it rained, she turned on the windshield wipers.
steps.zh: 下雨时，她打开了雨刮器。

notes.en: speed up = go faster.
notes.zh: speed up 就是开得更快。

notes.en: slow down = go slower.
notes.zh: slow down 就是开得更慢。

notes.en: Another way of saying press the accelerator is "step on the gas."
notes.zh: press the accelerator 的另一种说法是 step on the gas（踩油门）。

notes.en: Let up on the accelerator means "put less pressure on" it.
notes.zh: let up on the accelerator 意思是减轻油门上的压力，即松油门。

notes.en: Shifting gears is changing from one to another.
notes.zh: 换挡就是从一个挡位换到另一个挡位。

notes.en: Gears: 1=first, 2=second, 3=third, 4=fourth, R=reverse. Between gears is neutral.
notes.zh: 挡位：1 是一挡，2 是二挡，3 是三挡，4 是四挡，R 是倒挡；挡位之间为空挡。

china.en: In China, most drivers drive automatic cars, so they rarely use a clutch pedal or shift gears manually.
china.zh: 在中国，大多数人开自动挡汽车，因此很少用离合器踏板或手动换挡。

china.en: Chinese cars have the steering wheel on the left side, and drivers drive on the right side of the road.
china.zh: 中国汽车的方向盘在左侧，车辆靠右行驶。

grammarNote.en: The simple past is used for a sequence of driving events that happened and ended. Regular verbs: parked, pumped, checked, locked, stopped. Irregular verbs: drive-drove, get-got, give-gave, go-went, tell-told. Time markers: once, at the end of her trip, when the light turned green.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时用来描述一连串已经发生并结束的驾驶事件。规则动词：parked、pumped、checked、locked、stopped。不规则动词：drive-drove、get-got、give-gave、go-went、tell-told。时间标志词：once（有一次）、at the end of her trip（行程结束时）、when the light turned green（灯变绿时）。

steps.en: At an intersection Kate stopped for a red light.
steps.zh: 在十字路口，Kate 因红灯停了下来。

steps.en: When the light turned green, she went ahead.
steps.zh: 灯变绿时，她继续向前开。

steps.en: Once, she went over the speed limit.
A police officer stopped her and gave her a ticket.
steps.zh: 一位警察拦住她，给她开了罚单。

steps.en: At the end of her trip, she parked...
...and turned the car off.
Kate and her friends got out of the car...
...and Kate locked it.
Kate pulled into a gas station...
...and pulled up to a pump.
She told the attendant what kind of gas she wanted and how much.
steps.zh: 她告诉服务员要哪种汽油、加多少。

steps.en: He pumped the gas for her...
...and checked the oil.
Then she paid him.

notes.en: turn red = become red.
notes.zh: turn red 就是变红（指灯变红）。

notes.en: When speaking of cars, buses, etc.: pull in = drive in; pull up = drive forward; pull over = drive to the side of the road and stop.
notes.zh: 指汽车、公交车等时：pull in = 驶入；pull up = 向前开停住；pull over = 开到路边停下。

notes.en: To go over a limit is to go faster or farther than you should.
notes.zh: go over a limit 就是超出了应有的速度或距离，即超速。

china.en: In China, gas stations are often self-service or full-service; drivers usually pay inside the station or by scanning a QR code.
china.zh: 中国的加油站有自助也有全服务式；司机通常在站内付款或扫码支付。

china.en: Chinese expressways have toll gates where drivers pay by scanning an ETC card or stopping at a booth.
china.zh: 中国高速公路有收费站，司机通过 ETC 卡或停车缴费来付通行费。

china.en: Speed cameras and red-light cameras are common on Chinese roads, and fines are paid via phone apps.
china.zh: 中国道路上常见测速摄像头和闯红灯摄像头，罚款通过手机 App 缴纳。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tells the story of a train trip from buying a ticket to getting off. Regular verbs: announced, followed, inserted, opened, waited. Irregular verbs: buy-bought, get-got, have-had, stand-stood, take-took. Passive past (was crowded, was announced) also appears.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时讲述了从买票到下车的整个乘车过程。规则动词：announced、followed、inserted、opened、waited。不规则动词：buy-bought、get-got、have-had、stand-stood、take-took。本单元还出现了被动语态的过去式（was crowded 很挤、was announced 被广播）。

steps.en: Tom bought a ticket from the ticket machine.
steps.zh: Tom 从售票机买了一张票。

steps.en: Other passengers bought tickets at the ticket window.
steps.zh: 其他乘客在售票窗口买票。

steps.en: Tom inserted his ticket into the slot in the turnstile.
steps.zh: Tom 把票插进检票闸机的票口。

steps.en: The gate opened and Tom walked through.
steps.zh: 闸门打开，Tom 走了过去。

steps.en: He followed the signs to his gate.
steps.zh: 他跟着指示牌走到自己的检票口。

steps.en: He waited on the platform next to the track.
steps.zh: 他站在站台轨道旁等车。

steps.en: After his train arrived, he got on.
The train was crowded so he had to stand.
His station was announced...
...and he got off the train.

notes.en: The train was crowded. There were very many people in a small place.
notes.zh: 火车很拥挤，就是说一个很小的地方挤了很多人。

notes.en: When a gate with a turnstile opens, the turnstile rotates (turns).
notes.zh: 带闸机的检票口打开时，闸机会转动。

notes.en: If he had to stand, he could not find a place to sit.
notes.zh: 如果他只能站着，就是说找不到座位坐。

notes.en: His station was announced. This means someone announced his station.
notes.zh: 他要下的站被广播了，意思是有人广播了他那一站的名字。

notes.en: Other passengers are passengers who are not Tom.
notes.zh: "其他乘客"指的是除了 Tom 以外的乘客。

china.en: In China, most people buy train tickets on the 12306 phone app and use an ID card to pass through subway and train turnstiles.
china.zh: 在中国，大多数人在 12306 手机 App 上买火车票，刷身份证通过地铁和火车闸机。

china.en: High-speed trains (gaotie) are very popular in China, with trains reaching 350 km/h.
china.zh: 中国高铁非常普及，时速可达 350 公里。

china.en: Platform screen doors are installed on most subway platforms in Chinese cities.
china.zh: 中国城市的大多数地铁站台都装有屏蔽门。

grammarNote.en: The simple past narrates a short taxi ride. Regular verbs: hailed, started, checked, stopped. Irregular verbs: get-got into, give-gave, go-went, pay-paid, take-took, tell-told. The thought bubble "That's about right" shows a past judgment about the meter.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时讲述了一段短暂的打车经历。规则动词：hailed、started、checked、stopped。不规则动词：get-got into、give-gave、go-went、pay-paid、take-took、tell-told。思想泡泡里的 That's about right（差不多）是对计价器金额的过去判断。

steps.en: Pam hailed a taxi.
She got into the back seat...
...and told the driver where she wanted to go.
steps.zh: 然后告诉司机她要去哪里。

steps.en: He started the meter.
She checked the meter a few times.
During the ride, she gave the driver directions.
steps.zh: 乘车途中，她给司机指路。

steps.en: She told him where to stop.
steps.zh: 她告诉司机在哪里停车。

steps.en: She paid the fare and gave him a tip.
steps.zh: 她付了车费，并给了小费。

notes.en: To give directions means to tell someone how to get somewhere or how to do something.
notes.zh: give directions 就是告诉别人怎么去某个地方或怎么做某事。

notes.en: When you give someone a tip, you give them some extra money to thank them for good service.
notes.zh: 给小费就是多给一点钱，感谢对方提供的好服务。

notes.en: Other ways to say hail a taxi are: "Wave for a taxi," "Wave down a taxi," "Flag down a taxi."
notes.zh: hail a taxi 的其他说法有：Wave for a taxi、Wave down a taxi、Flag down a taxi（都是挥手叫出租车）。

notes.en: Taxis that pass by go past someone without stopping.
notes.zh: pass by 的出租车就是开过身边却不停的出租车。

notes.en: To check the meter is to look quickly at it to see what it says.
notes.zh: 看计价器就是快速瞥一眼上面显示的金额。

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: I need to go to Riverside Square.

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: Turn left at the next traffic light.

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: Pull over by that red car.
dialogue.zh: 在那辆红车旁边靠边停。

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: Here's six-twenty plus a little extra for you.
dialogue.zh: 这是六块二，另外多给你一点。

china.en: In China, people rarely hail taxis on the street; they use apps like Didi (DiDi Chuxing) to book rides.
china.zh: 在中国，人们很少在路边招手叫出租车，而是用滴滴出行等 App 叫车。

china.en: Chinese taxi drivers and passengers usually do not give or expect tips.
china.zh: 中国出租车司机和乘客一般不给、也不期望小费。

china.en: Rides are often paid automatically through the app linked to a mobile wallet, no cash needed.
china.zh: 车费通常通过绑定手机钱包的 App 自动支付，无需现金。

grammarNote.en: The simple past describes a person's walking trip through the neighborhood. Regular verbs: walked, stepped, stopped, waited, crossed, used. Irregular verbs: run-ran, take-took. Time adverbs: once, sometimes, when he could.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时描述一个人步行穿过街区的过程。规则动词：walked、stepped、stopped、waited、crossed、used。不规则动词：run-ran、take-took。时间副词：once（有一次）、sometimes（有时）、when he could（来得及的时候）。

steps.en: Dan walked on the sidewalk.
Sometimes he stepped over dirt or puddles.
steps.zh: 有时他跨过泥土或水坑。

steps.en: Once, he tripped on a crack in the sidewalk.
steps.zh: 有一次，他被人行道上的裂缝绊了一下。

steps.en: At a corner, he stopped at the curb and waited for traffic to pass.
steps.zh: 在街角，他在路缘石边停下，等车辆通过。

steps.en: Then he crossed the street by walking in the crosswalk.
steps.zh: 然后他走斑马线过了马路。

steps.en: Once he took a shortcut across a parking lot.
steps.zh: 有一次他抄近路穿过一个停车场。

steps.en: When he could, he ran because he was late.
steps.zh: 来得及的时候他就跑，因为要迟到了。

steps.en: He crossed a busy street by using a pedestrian overpass.
steps.zh: 他走人行天桥穿过一条繁忙的马路。

notes.en: A sidewalk is a paved (concrete) place for walking.
notes.zh: 人行道是铺好（水泥）的走路地方。

notes.en: traffic = the group of cars, trucks, buses, bikes, etc., on a street.
notes.zh: traffic 指街上行驶的汽车、卡车、公交车、自行车等的总称。

notes.en: When you take a shortcut, you use a shorter way than the usual way.
notes.zh: 走捷径就是走一条比平时更短的路。

notes.en: a pedestrian = someone who is walking.
notes.zh: pedestrian 就是正在走路的人，即行人。

notes.en: An overpass is a bridge for passing over the street.
notes.zh: overpass 是供人横穿街道上方的桥，即人行天桥。

china.en: In China, pedestrians often use subway crossings or footbridges instead of jaywalking, and many intersections have countdown traffic lights.
china.zh: 在中国，行人通常走地下通道或人行天桥，而不是乱穿马路；很多路口有红绿灯倒计时。

china.en: Chinese cities have sidewalks and bike lanes, but sidewalks are sometimes blocked by e-bikes or street vendors.
china.zh: 中国城市有人行道和自行车道，但人行道有时会被电动车或摊贩占用。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tells a first-person bike ride story. Regular verbs: started, moved, shifted, squeezed, locked. Irregular verbs: get-got off, hold-held, put-put, ride-rode, swing-swung. The first-person "I" makes the past actions immediate and personal.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时以第一人称讲述一次骑自行车的经历。规则动词：started、moved、shifted、squeezed、locked。不规则动词：get-got off、hold-held、put-put、ride-rode、swing-swung。第一人称 I 让过去的动作显得直接、亲切。

steps.en: I put on my helmet.
I held the handlebars...
...and swung my leg over the bike.
I started pedaling and the bike moved.
steps.zh: 我开始蹬踏板，自行车动了起来。

steps.en: To go uphill,...
...I shifted into a lower gear.
To slow down, I squeezed the brakes.
Finally, I got off my bike...
...and locked it up in a bike rack.
steps.zh: 然后把它锁在自行车架上。

notes.en: A helmet is a very hard hat that protects your head.
notes.zh: 头盔是很硬的帽子，用来保护头部。

notes.en: The parts of a bike where your feet are the pedals. You pedal the bike by pushing on the pedals.
notes.zh: 自行车上放脚的地方叫踏板，蹬踏板就是骑车。

notes.en: When you squeeze something, you grip it tightly.
notes.zh: squeeze 就是紧紧握住、捏紧。

notes.en: When you shift gears, you change from one to another.
notes.zh: 换挡就是从一个挡位换到另一个挡位。

china.en: In China, shared bikes (like Meituan and HelloBike) are very popular; people scan a QR code to unlock them and park in designated zones.
china.zh: 在中国，共享单车（如美团、哈啰）非常流行；人们扫码解锁，停在指定区域即可。

china.en: Chinese cities have dedicated bike lanes, but e-bikes are also very common and often share the lane.
china.zh: 中国城市有专用自行车道，但电动车也很常见，常与自行车共用非机动车道。

china.en: Wearing a helmet is required or strongly recommended for e-bike riders in many Chinese cities.
china.zh: 中国很多城市要求或强烈建议电动车骑行者戴头盔。

grammarNote.en: Most of the verbs in 'At Home in the Evening' are in the simple past tense (e.g. got, checked, took, walked, opened). Some verbs also appear in their '-ing' form acting as nouns (pressing, waiting) or adjectives (answering machine).
grammarNote.zh: “晚间在家”这一部分的动词大多使用一般过去时（如 got、checked、took、walked、opened）。有些动词以 -ing 形式出现，作动名词（pressing、waiting）或形容词（answering machine 答录机）。

steps.en: Dan got back to his building.
steps.zh: 丹回到了他住的公寓楼。

steps.en: He checked his mailbox and took out his mail.
steps.zh: 他看了看信箱，取出了信件。

steps.en: Then he took an elevator up to his floor.
steps.zh: 然后他乘电梯上到自己住的楼层。

steps.en: He walked down the hall to his apartment.
steps.zh: 他走过走廊，来到自己的公寓门前。

steps.en: He opened his door and went inside.
To take an elevator: press the 'up' button and wait for the elevator.
steps.zh: 乘电梯时：按下“上行”按钮，等待电梯到来。

steps.en: Get on the elevator, choose a floor, and get off at your floor.
steps.zh: 走进电梯，选择楼层，到达后走出电梯。

steps.en: I got back to my house and walked up the steps to my front door.
steps.zh: 我回到家，走上台阶来到前门。

steps.en: I unlocked the door with my house key and opened it by turning the doorknob.
steps.zh: 我用钥匙打开门锁，转动门把手推开门。

steps.en: I set my bag down and hung my coat up in the front closet.
steps.zh: 我把包放下，把外套挂进门前的衣帽间。

steps.en: I took off my shoes and picked up my mail.
Then I went into the living room and checked for messages on the answering machine.
steps.zh: 然后我走进客厅，查看答录机里的留言。

steps.en: I took off my work clothes and changed into some casual clothes.
steps.zh: 我脱下工作服，换上便装。

notes.en: get back = return
notes.zh: get back 意思就是 return（回到）。

notes.en: You take an elevator just as you take a bus; you use it to get somewhere.
notes.zh: 乘电梯和乘公共汽车一样，都是借它到达某个地方。

notes.en: Most of the verbs in 'At Home in the Evening' are in the simple past tense.
notes.zh: “晚间在家”部分的动词大多用一般过去时。

notes.en: Some verbs appear in the '-ing' form acting as nouns (pressing, waiting) or adjectives (answering in answering machine).
notes.zh: 有些动词以 -ing 形式作动名词（pressing 按、waiting 等待）或形容词（answering machine 中的 answering）。

china.en: In China most apartment buildings have elevators, and residents often use a key card or password instead of a metal mailbox key to enter.
china.zh: 在中国，多数公寓楼都有电梯；居民进单元门常用门禁卡或密码，而不是用钥匙开楼下信箱。

china.en: Few homes in China still use answering machines; people check voice mail or WeChat messages on their phones.
china.zh: 中国家庭现在很少使用电话答录机，人们直接在手机上听语音留言或看微信消息。

china.en: Many Chinese homeowners take off their shoes at the door and wear indoor slippers, just as shown here.
china.zh: 很多中国人进门也会换拖鞋，和图里进门脱鞋的习惯类似。

grammarNote.en: The narration uses the simple past (rinsed, drained, sliced, mixed, laid, sprinkled, poured) to describe a sequence of completed actions in the kitchen.
grammarNote.zh: 叙述使用一般过去时（rinsed 冲洗、drained 沥干、sliced 切片、mixed 混合、laid 摆放、sprinkled 撒、poured 浇），描述厨房里一连串已完成的动作。

steps.en: Paul rinsed some lettuce by running water over it, and drained it in a colander.
steps.zh: 保罗用水冲洗生菜，然后放在滤水篮里沥干。

steps.en: He also rinsed some tomatoes and cucumbers, and sliced them with a knife on a cutting board.
steps.zh: 他又冲洗了西红柿和黄瓜，在砧板上用刀切片。

steps.en: He mixed the lettuce and the cucumber in a salad bowl, and laid the tomato slices on top.
steps.zh: 他把生菜和黄瓜在沙拉碗里拌匀，再把西红柿片摆在上层。

steps.en: Then he sprinkled some grated cheese on the salad.
steps.zh: 接着他在沙拉上撒了一些擦碎的奶酪。

steps.en: He poured some dressing on his salad.
steps.zh: 他又在沙拉上浇了一些沙拉酱。

notes.en: 'On top' means 'on the top of' something we already know. Example: 'a bus with a sign on top' = 'on top of the bus.'
notes.zh: on top 指“在我们已知事物的顶部”。例如“车顶有标志的公交车”即 on top of the bus。

notes.en: Paul rinsed the lettuce. You can also say 'Paul washed some lettuce.'
notes.zh: Paul rinsed the lettuce. 也可以说成 Paul washed some lettuce.

notes.en: You drain something by letting water go off it or out of it.
notes.zh: drain（沥干）就是让水从食物上流走或漏掉。

notes.en: Grated cheese has been cut or shaved into very small pieces with a grater.
notes.zh: grated cheese（擦碎的奶酪）是用擦板把奶酪切成很细的屑。

notes.en: When you sprinkle something, you spread small amounts of a liquid or solid over a wide area.
notes.zh: sprinkle（撒）指把少量液体或固体均匀地撒在一大片表面上。

china.en: Chinese home cooking rarely uses western salad dressing; cold dishes are usually tossed with soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and chili oil.
china.zh: 中国家庭很少用西式沙拉酱，凉菜一般用酱油、醋、蒜末、辣椒油凉拌。

china.en: Iceberg lettuce is now common in Chinese supermarkets, but many families still prefer to blanch vegetables instead of eating them raw.
china.zh: 现在超市能买到西生菜，但很多中国人仍习惯把蔬菜焯水后再吃，而不是生吃。

china.en: A 'salad spinner' or colander is less common in Chinese kitchens; people usually just shake the washed greens in a basket.
china.zh: 中国家庭里沙拉脱水篮不太常见，洗好的菜一般放在菜筐里自然沥干。

grammarNote.en: Simple past narration (peeled, sliced, chopped, threw, rinsed, put, lit, boiled, steamed) describes a sequence of cooking actions.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（peeled 削皮、sliced 切片、chopped 切块、threw 扔掉、rinsed 冲洗、put 放、lit 点燃、boiled 煮开、steamed 蒸）叙述一系列做菜动作。

steps.en: Kate peeled some carrots and sliced them.
steps.zh: 凯特给胡萝卜去皮，然后切成片。

steps.en: She also chopped up some broccoli and threw the stalk away.
steps.zh: 她还把西兰花切成小朵，把菜梗扔掉。

steps.en: She rinsed the broccoli and put some water in a saucepan.
steps.zh: 她把西兰花冲洗干净，在汤锅里加了些水。

steps.en: She put a steamer basket inside, then put the vegetables in the basket.
steps.zh: 她在锅里放上蒸格，再把蔬菜放进蒸格。

steps.en: She put a lid on the saucepan and lit the burner under it.
The water boiled and steamed the vegetables.
steps.zh: 水烧开后，蒸汽把菜蒸熟了。

notes.en: When you steam something, you put it above—but not in—boiling water. The steam rises and cooks the food.
notes.zh: 蒸菜时把食物放在沸水上方（但不泡在水里），蒸汽上升把食物蒸熟。

notes.en: Slice means cutting into thin, flat pieces with a smooth, gentle motion. Chop means cutting into irregular pieces by cutting forcefully.
notes.zh: slice（切片）是用平稳、轻柔的动作切成薄而平的片；chop（切块）是用力切成不规则的小块。

china.en: Steaming is one of the most common cooking methods in Chinese kitchens; bamboo steamers are widely used instead of metal steamer baskets.
china.zh: 蒸是中国厨房里最常见的做法之一，常用竹制蒸笼而不是金属蒸格。

china.en: Chinese homes almost always use a gas stove or induction cooktop; the burner being lit here looks the same.
china.zh: 中国家庭几乎都用燃气灶或电磁炉，图里点燃炉头的样子和国内一样。

china.en: Stir-frying (chǎo) is far more common than steaming for dinner vegetables; steaming is usually reserved for fish, buns or dumplings.
china.zh: 晚餐蔬菜更多是大火快炒，蒸菜通常留给鱼、包子或饺子。

grammarNote.en: The whole recipe is narrated in the simple past (diced, fried, stirred, heated, added, boiled, drained, ladled). Some verbs also have active intransitive uses such as 'the meat fried' and 'the water boiled.'
grammarNote.zh: 整个食谱都用一般过去时叙述（diced 切丁、fried 煎、stirred 翻炒、heated 加热、added 加入、boiled 煮、drained 沥干、ladled 舀浇）。有些动词也作不及物动词用，如 the meat fried（肉煎着）、the water boiled（水煮开了）。

steps.en: Kate diced an onion and fried it with some ground beef in a frying pan.
steps.zh: 凯特把洋葱切丁，和牛肉末一起在煎锅里炒。

steps.en: As the beef-and-onion mixture fried, she stirred it; when the meat was brown, she turned off the burner.
steps.zh: 牛肉洋葱馅在锅里炒时她不停翻炒；肉变色后她关掉炉火。

steps.en: She poured the fat into a can and heated two cans of tomato sauce in a saucepan.
steps.zh: 她把多余的油沥到罐子里，再在汤锅里热两罐番茄酱。

steps.en: She added the mixture of beef and onions, and stirred it into the sauce with some spices.
steps.zh: 她把牛肉洋葱馅倒进番茄酱，加一些香料搅拌均匀。

steps.en: When it started to boil, she turned down the heat and let the sauce simmer.
steps.zh: 酱汁煮开后，她把火调小，让酱汁小火慢炖。

steps.en: In another pan, she boiled some water and put some spaghetti into the boiling water.
steps.zh: 在另一口锅里烧开水，把意大利面放进去煮。

steps.en: She boiled the spaghetti until it was tender, then drained it in a colander.
steps.zh: 把面煮到变软，再倒入滤水篮沥干。

steps.en: After putting the spaghetti on a plate, she ladled some sauce over it.
steps.zh: 把面盛到盘子里，用勺子浇上酱汁。

notes.en: Ground beef is meat from a cow that has been ground into small pieces.
notes.zh: ground beef（牛绞肉）是把牛肉绞成碎末。

notes.en: Fat is an oily part of meat; it becomes liquid when the meat cooks.
notes.zh: fat（油脂）是肉里出油的部分，加热后会变成液体。

notes.en: To separate a liquid from a solid, you can pour off the liquid or drain the solid.
notes.zh: 要把液体和固体分开，可以 pour off（倒掉液体）或 drain（滤掉液体）。

notes.en: Spaghetti is a kind of noodle. Oregano and basil are common spices in spaghetti sauce.
notes.zh: spaghetti 是一种面条。牛至（oregano）和罗勒（basil）是意面酱里常用的香料。

notes.en: A liquid simmers when it cooks slowly and gently. If spaghetti is tender, it is soft enough to eat.
notes.zh: simmer（文火慢炖）是小火慢慢煮。面煮到 tender（软嫩）就可以吃了。

notes.en: You ladle sauce onto spaghetti when you use a ladle to pour it on.
notes.zh: ladle sauce onto spaghetti 就是用长勺把酱汁浇在面上。

china.en: Spaghetti Bolognese is popular in big cities in China, but at home most Chinese families stir-fry noodles or make tomato-and-egg noodles instead.
china.zh: 意大利肉酱面在大城市流行，但中国家庭自己做时更多是炒面或西红柿鸡蛋打卤面。

china.en: Ground beef is readily available in Chinese supermarkets, but fresh tomatoes or tomato paste are often used instead of canned tomato sauce.
china.zh: 超市能买到牛肉末，但一般用新鲜番茄或番茄酱，而不是罐装意面酱。

china.en: Chinese kitchens usually use a wok (炒锅) for frying, not a flat frying pan like the one in the picture.
china.zh: 中国厨房炒菜一般用中式炒锅，而不是图里这种平底煎锅。

grammarNote.en: Simple past narration (measured, poured, rinsed, heated, turned down, checked, decided) describes how rice was cooked on the stove.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（measured 量、poured 倒、rinsed 淘洗、heated 加热、turned down 调小、checked 查看、decided 判断）讲述在炉子上煮饭的过程。

steps.en: Paul measured out one cup of rice and poured it into a pot.
steps.zh: 保罗量出一杯米，倒进锅里。

steps.en: To rinse the rice, he put some water in the pot and poured off the water to get rid of the dirt and husks.
steps.zh: 为了淘米，他在锅里加水，再把水倒掉，冲掉米里的灰尘和米糠。

steps.en: Then he measured out two cups of clean water and poured it into the pot.
steps.zh: 然后他量出两杯清水，倒进锅里。

steps.en: He put a lid on the pot and heated the water.
When it started boiling, he turned down the flame.
After about 15 minutes, he checked the rice and decided it was ready to eat.
steps.zh: 大约 15 分钟后，他打开锅盖查看，判断饭已经好了。

notes.en: You measure out an exact amount of something.
notes.zh: measure out 指量出一个准确的量。

notes.en: A husk is the skin around a grain of rice.
notes.zh: husk（谷壳）是包裹在米粒外面的皮。

notes.en: be done = be finished. Food that is done is fully cooked.
notes.zh: be done 意思就是 be finished（做好了）；食物 done 就是完全煮熟了。

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.en: Let's see if this is ready.

china.en: Almost every Chinese household uses an electric rice cooker (电饭煲) instead of cooking rice on the stove; the cooker switches itself off when the rice is done.
china.zh: 几乎每个中国家庭都用电饭煲煮饭，而不是在炉子上看火；饭好了电饭煲会自动跳闸。

china.en: Rinsing the rice by hand is still common in China, but many people now just buy pre-washed rice.
china.zh: 淘米在中国仍然很常见，但现在也有很多人直接买免淘米。

china.en: The water-to-rice ratio is often judged by finger depth rather than measuring cups.
china.zh: 水量通常用手指量米水面高度来判断，而不是用量杯。

grammarNote.en: Simple past (sat down, put, helped, passed, ate, talked, had) describes the whole dinner sequence. Note set the table uses the fixed expression 'set a table.'
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（sat down 坐下、put 放、helped oneself 自取、passed 递、ate 吃、talked 聊天、had 吃）描述整个晚餐过程。注意摆桌固定说法是 set a table。

steps.en: Paul and Kate set the table. Everyone sat down at the table.
steps.zh: 保罗和凯特别摆好餐具，大家在餐桌旁坐下。

steps.en: They put their napkins on their laps.
Paul helped himself to some salad and passed the serving dish to Kate.
steps.zh: 保罗自己盛了一些沙拉，然后把菜盘递给凯特。

steps.en: Then they helped themselves to the food.
steps.zh: 接着大家各自夹取想吃的菜。

steps.en: As they ate, they talked.
Paul had a second helping of spaghetti.
steps.zh: 保罗又添了一份意大利面。

steps.en: After the main course, they had some dessert.
steps.zh: 主菜吃完后，他们吃了些甜点。

notes.en: help yourself = take something for yourself.
notes.zh: help yourself 意思是自己动手拿（食物），别客气。

notes.en: In a meal, a helping is the amount you take to eat.
notes.zh: 一顿饭里的 helping 指你一次盛到的那份量。

notes.en: Your lap is the upper part of your legs when you are sitting down.
notes.zh: lap 指坐下时大腿上方摊开的部位。

dialogue.speaker: 家人
dialogue.en: So, where did you go today?

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.en: I'll have a bit more of this.

china.en: Chinese dinner tables usually have shared dishes in the middle and everyone uses chopsticks; napkins on laps are rare, paper tissues are common.
china.zh: 中式晚餐一般是菜放中间、大家用筷子夹菜；很少把餐巾铺在腿上，更多是用纸巾。

china.en: A separate 'main course then dessert' order is not typical in China; all dishes are served at once and fruit often comes after the meal.
china.zh: 中式晚餐不讲究“主菜后甜点”的顺序，菜一起上，饭后常吃点水果。

china.en: When Chinese people want more food they often say '再添点饭' rather than help themselves without asking.
china.zh: 中国人添饭时常会说“再给我盛点饭”，而不是默不作声地自己加。

grammarNote.en: Simple past (offered, stacked, carried, took, put, scraped, wiped, threw) describes cleaning up after dinner.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（offered 主动提出、stacked 摞起、carried 端走、took 拿走、put 放、scraped 刮、wiped 擦、threw 扔）描述饭后收拾餐桌的过程。

steps.en: After everyone was done, Paul and Kate offered to clear the table.
steps.zh: 大家吃完后，保罗和凯特主动提出收拾桌子。

steps.en: They stacked up the dirty dishes and carried them to the kitchen.
steps.zh: 他们把脏盘子摞起来，端到厨房。

steps.en: They took the serving dishes off the table and put the leftovers into containers, which they put into the refrigerator.
steps.zh: 他们把大盘子端下餐桌，把剩菜装进保鲜盒，再放进冰箱。

steps.en: They scraped the scraps from the plates into the garbage.
steps.zh: 他们把盘子里的残渣刮进垃圾桶。

steps.en: Then they wiped the table off and threw the scraps and crumbs from the table into the garbage.
steps.zh: 然后把桌子擦干净，把桌上的残渣和面包屑也扫进垃圾桶。

notes.en: If you offer to do something, you say you'll do it even though no one asked you to.
notes.zh: offer to do something 指没人请你，你也主动说要去做。

notes.en: Leftovers are amounts of food to keep after a dinner.
notes.zh: leftovers 指饭后留下来的剩菜。

notes.en: Crumbs (small pieces of bread) and scraps are pieces of food to throw away after a dinner.
notes.zh: crumbs（面包屑）和 scraps（食物残渣）是饭后要扔掉的零碎食物。

notes.en: You stack things up by putting them on top of one another. You are done eating when you have finished your meal.
notes.zh: stack up 就是把东西一个摞一个。吃完饭就说 you are done eating。

dialogue.speaker: Kate
dialogue.en: Paul and I will clear up.

dialogue.speaker: Paul
dialogue.en: Yeah. The rest of you just sit and relax.
dialogue.zh: 对，你们其他人坐着歇会儿吧。

china.en: In many Chinese families, one person (often the mother or whoever cooked) clears the table; using plastic food containers (保鲜盒) for leftovers is also very common.
china.zh: 中国家庭饭后通常由一个人（常是做饭的妈妈）收拾；用保鲜盒装剩菜放进冰箱也很普遍。

china.en: Chinese homes usually have a kitchen waste (湿垃圾) and other waste (干垃圾) sorting bin, especially in cities like Beijing and Shanghai.
china.zh: 现在中国城市（如北京、上海）家里一般会把厨余垃圾和其他垃圾分类装桶。

china.en: Leftovers are often eaten for the next day's lunch, rather than being thrown away.
china.zh: 剩菜常常留到第二天中午热一热再吃，而不是直接扔掉。

grammarNote.en: Simple past (put, filled, washed, scrubbed, rinsed, pulled, dried) describes the whole hand-washing-dishes routine.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（put 塞、filled 放水、washed 洗、scrubbed 用力刷、rinsed 冲净、pulled 拔、dried 擦干）描述整套手洗碗筷的流程。

steps.en: Paul put the plug into the drain in the sink and filled the sink with water.
steps.zh: 保罗把水槽塞子塞好，往水槽里放满水。

steps.en: He put some dish soap into the water.
steps.zh: 他在水里挤了些洗洁精。

steps.en: He washed the dirty dishes with a dishcloth, and scrubbed some very dirty dishes with a scrubbing pad.
steps.zh: 他用洗碗布洗脏盘子，特别脏的地方用百洁布刷一刷。

steps.en: Then he rinsed the dishes.
steps.zh: 然后他把碗碟冲洗干净。

steps.en: He put the wet dishes in the dish rack, where the water dripped off them.
steps.zh: 他把湿碗碟放进碗架，让水沥掉。

steps.en: Then he pulled the plug from the sink and the dirty water went down the drain.
steps.zh: 接着他拔出水槽塞子，脏水流进下水道。

steps.en: He dried the dishes with a dish towel and put the dishes away in the cupboard.
steps.zh: 他用抹布把碗碟擦干，再放进碗橱收好。

notes.en: Dish soap is also called 'detergent.'
notes.zh: dish soap 也叫 detergent（洗涤剂）。

notes.en: You scrub something by rubbing very hard and for a long time as you wash it.
notes.zh: scrub（用力刷）指洗碗时使劲、长时间地摩擦。

notes.en: Water that goes down the drain is gone. 'Down the drain' is used to mean 'wasted' or 'gone': 'All his hard work went down the drain.'
notes.zh: 水流进下水道就没了。down the drain 引申为“白费、付诸东流”，比如 All his hard work went down the drain.（他的努力全白费了。）

china.en: Dishwashers are still not common in Chinese homes; most people wash dishes by hand at the kitchen sink.
china.zh: 洗碗机在中国家庭里还不普及，大多数人还是在水槽边手洗碗筷。

china.en: Chinese kitchens usually have a two-compartment sink with hot water on tap; a dish rack near the window is very common.
china.zh: 中国厨房一般是双槽洗菜池，有热水；窗边放个沥水碗架也很常见。

china.en: Dish soap is usually called 'xiéjīng (洗洁精)' in Chinese; people also use baking soda or hot water to cut grease.
china.zh: 洗洁精中文就叫“洗洁精”；去油重时也会用热水或小苏打。

grammarNote.en: Simple past narration (chose, put on, pressed, listened, paused, stopped, put down) describes listening to songs on a phone in the evening.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（chose 选择、put on 戴上、pressed 按下、listened 听、paused 暂停、stopped 停止、put down 放下）描述晚上用手机听歌的过程。

steps.en: I chose a song on my mom's phone.
steps.zh: 我在妈妈手机上选了一首歌。

steps.en: I put on my earphones.
I pressed play.
I listened to the music.
When Dad called me, I pressed pause.
steps.zh: 爸爸叫我时，我按了暂停。

steps.en: Then I pressed play again.
At night, I stopped the music and put the phone down.
steps.zh: 晚上，我停掉音乐，把手机放下。

notes.en: A music app on the phone, like QQ Music or NetEase Cloud Music, lets you choose songs and press play.
notes.zh: 手机上的音乐 App（如 QQ 音乐、网易云音乐）可以让你选歌并按下播放。

notes.en: Pause means to stop for a short time. You can press play again to continue.
notes.zh: pause 是暂停一会儿，再按播放键可以继续。

notes.en: Put on your earphones before you press play, so the music is only for you.
notes.zh: 按播放前先戴上耳机，这样音乐只属于你自己。

china.en: In China, children listen to songs and audio stories on their parents' phones with apps like QQ Music and NetEase Cloud Music.
china.zh: 在中国，孩子常用爸爸妈妈的手机，通过 QQ 音乐、网易云音乐等 App 听歌和听故事。

china.en: Many Chinese families limit screen time for kids, so the phone is often Mom or Dad's, not the child's own.
china.zh: 很多中国家庭会控制孩子看屏幕的时间，手机通常是爸爸妈妈的，不是孩子自己的。

units.en: Listening to Music on a Phone

grammarNote.en: Simple past (put on, chose, pressed, turned up, turned down, listened, took off) describes listening to songs with earphones on a phone.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（put on 戴上、chose 选择、pressed 按下、turned up 调大、turned down 调小、listened 听、took off 摘下）描述戴耳机用手机听歌的过程。

steps.en: I put on my earphones.
I chose a song on the phone.
steps.zh: 我在手机上选了一首歌。

steps.en: I pressed play.
I turned the volume up a little to hear it better.
steps.zh: 我把音量调大一点，听得更清楚。

steps.en: Then I turned it down a little.
I listened to the songs for a while.
When I finished, I took off my earphones.

notes.en: Turn up means to make the sound louder. Turn down means to make the sound softer.
notes.zh: turn up 是把声音调大，turn down 是把声音调小。

notes.en: Wearing earphones helps others in the room enjoy quiet. You hear the music only yourself.
notes.zh: 戴上耳机不会吵到房间里的其他人，音乐只属于你自己。

notes.en: Too much loud music is bad for your ears, so keep the volume low.
notes.zh: 音乐太响会伤耳朵，所以要控制音量。

china.en: In China, most people listen to music with Bluetooth earphones or earbuds; wired earphone jacks are disappearing from new phones.
china.zh: 在中国，大家主要用蓝牙耳机听歌，新手机几乎没有了耳机孔。

china.en: Kids' listening time on the phone is often limited by parents, for eye and ear health.
china.zh: 为了保护视力和听力，中国家长常会限制孩子用手机听音频的时间。

grammarNote.en: Simple past (opened, turned, saw, looked up, finished, closed, picked up, flipped through, found, read) describes reading a book and a magazine.
grammarNote.zh: 用一般过去时（opened 打开、turned 翻页、saw 看到、looked up 查阅、finished 读完、closed 合上、picked up 拿起、flipped through 快速翻、found 找到、read 读）描述看书和翻杂志的过程。

steps.en: Pam opened the book to her bookmark and turned the pages as she read.
steps.zh: 帕姆打开书，翻到夹着书签的那一页，一边读一边翻页。

steps.en: When she saw a word she didn't know, she looked it up in a dictionary.
steps.zh: 遇到不认识的词，她就查词典。

steps.en: When she finished reading, she closed the book.
Pam picked up the latest issue of Everyone magazine.
steps.zh: 帕姆拿起最新一期 Everyone 杂志。

steps.en: She looked at some of the ads, then flipped through the magazine until she found an interesting article.
steps.zh: 她先看了几眼广告，然后快速翻页，直到看到一篇感兴趣的文章。

steps.en: She read the article and looked at the pictures.
steps.zh: 她读了那篇文章，还看了配图。

notes.en: If you flip through something, you turn its pages or parts quickly.
notes.zh: flip through 指很快地翻书页或翻杂志。

notes.en: An interesting thing is one you want to see, hear, read, or do.
notes.zh: interesting 就是让你想看、想听、想读、想做的事。

notes.en: 'Ad' is a short form of 'advertisement.'
notes.zh: ad 是 advertisement（广告）的缩写。

notes.en: To look up a word, you find it in a dictionary and read its meaning.
notes.zh: look up a word 指在词典里查到这个词并读它的意思。

notes.en: If a magazine comes out every month, each month there is a new issue—the January issue, February issue, etc.
notes.zh: 如果杂志每月出一期，每个月就有新的 issue（一期），比如一月号、二月号。

china.en: Many Chinese now read novels and news on their phones or e-readers (like Kindle or WeChat Read) instead of physical books.
china.zh: 现在很多中国人用手机或电子书（如微信读书）看小说、看新闻，纸质书看得少了。

china.en: Printed magazines have declined sharply in China; people read short video content and WeChat public accounts instead.
china.zh: 中国的纸质杂志大幅减少，大家更多刷短视频、看微信公众号文章。

china.en: When meeting an unknown English word, Chinese learners usually look it up in a dictionary app on the phone rather than a printed dictionary.
china.zh: 遇到不认识的英文单词，中国学生一般用手机词典 App 查，而不是翻纸质词典。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions that happened and finished at a specific time in the past. Regular verbs add -ed (e.g., watched, turned), while irregular verbs change form (e.g., go→went). / 一般过去时描述在过去某个特定时间发生并已完成的动作。规则动词加 -ed（如 watched、turned），不规则动词则改变形式（如 go→went）。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: Tom picked up the remote for the TV...
...and turned the TV on.
A game show was on.
steps.zh: 一个游戏节目正在播出。

steps.en: Tom didn't want to watch it...
...so he used the remote...
...to change channels.
He turned up the volume so he could hear better.
steps.zh: 他调大了音量，以便听得更清楚。

steps.en: During a commercial...
...he went to the kitchen for a snack.
He watched the news,...
...and when it ended,...
...he turned the TV off.

notes.en: TV is a short way of saying "television."
notes.zh: TV 是 television 的简称。

notes.en: Tom says a show is boring. That means it is not interesting.
notes.zh: 汤姆说节目很无聊，意思是这个节目没意思。

notes.en: A commercial is advertising on TV or radio.
notes.zh: 商业广告是电视或广播上播出的广告。

notes.en: The news is a report about what has happened. It always has an "s" at the end.
notes.zh: news 是关于所发生事情的报道，词尾总是带 "s"。

notes.en: TVs have channels while radios have stations.
notes.zh: 电视机有频道（channels），而收音机有电台（stations）。

notes.en: A remote is also called a remote control.
notes.zh: remote 也叫作 remote control。

dialogue.speaker: game show host
dialogue.en: Now, for fifty-three dollars, what's the name of...
dialogue.zh: 现在，为了五十三美元，它叫什么名字……

dialogue.speaker: news anchor
dialogue.en: That's the end of the news.

china.en: In China, most people watch shows through streaming apps on smart TVs or phones (like iQiyi and Youku) rather than tuning into over-the-air channels.
china.zh: 在中国，大多数人通过智能电视或手机上的流媒体应用（如爱奇艺、优酷）追剧，而不是调传统电视频道。

china.en: Chinese families often eat sunflower seeds or drink tea while watching TV together in the living room.
china.zh: 中国家庭在客厅一起看电视时，常嗑瓜子或喝茶当零食。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions: chose, pressed, watched, replayed, paused, stopped, closed. Irregular verbs: choose→chose, see→saw.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时描述已完成的动作：chose、pressed、watched、replayed、paused、stopped、closed。不规则动词：choose→chose。

steps.en: Jenny chose a cartoon on the tablet.
steps.zh: 珍妮在平板上选了一部动画片。

steps.en: She pressed play.
She and Tom watched the video.
To see something again, she tapped replay.
steps.zh: 为了再看一遍某段，她点了重播。

steps.en: Jenny paused it when Mom called her.
steps.zh: 妈妈叫她时，珍妮按了暂停。

steps.en: At the end of the video, she stopped it.
steps.zh: 视频结束时，她按了停止。

steps.en: She closed the app and put the tablet down.

notes.en: Replay means to play something again from the beginning or from where you tapped.
notes.zh: replay 是从头或从你点的地方再播放一遍。

notes.en: When you pause a video, the picture stops but stays on the screen. Press play to go on.
notes.zh: 暂停视频时画面停下来但还在屏幕上，按播放键继续。

notes.en: Watching too long is bad for your eyes. Take a break after a while.
notes.zh: 看太久伤眼睛，看一会儿要休息一下。

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: I'd like to see that again.

china.en: In China, kids watch cartoons on a tablet or phone with apps like iQiyi Kids, Tencent Video, or Bilibili; video stores are long gone.
china.zh: 在中国，孩子用平板或手机在爱奇艺儿童、腾讯视频、哔哩哔哩等应用上看动画片，实体影碟店早已消失。

china.en: Many Chinese parents set a screen-time limit and a kids mode on the tablet.
china.zh: 很多中国家长会给平板设置使用时长限制和儿童模式。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions in the past. Many verbs here are irregular: babysit→babysat, draw→drew, put→put, read→read, take→took. / 一般过去时描述过去已完成的动作。本单元很多动词是不规则的：babysit→babysat、draw→drew、put→put、read→read、take→took。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: Tom babysat his cousins — took care of them while their parents were gone.
steps.zh: 汤姆照看他的表兄妹——在他们父母不在时照顾他们。

steps.en: Tom's aunt and uncle dropped the children off at Tom's house.
steps.zh: 汤姆的姑姑和姑父把孩子送到汤姆家。

steps.en: Tom took them to a playground.
Back at Tom's house, they played with blocks,...
steps.zh: 回到汤姆家，他们玩积木……

steps.en: ...drew pictures with crayons...
...and put a puzzle together.
Tom changed the baby's diaper...
...and put him to bed in the crib.
steps.zh: 然后把他放进婴儿床睡觉。

steps.en: The other children took a bath.
Tom read them a story...
...and they watched a cartoon on TV.
steps.zh: 然后他们在电视上看动画片。

steps.en: Later, their parents picked the children up.
steps.zh: 后来，他们的父母来接走了孩子。

notes.en: "Kids" is an informal word for children.
notes.zh: kids 是 children 的非正式说法。

notes.en: Tom's aunt is his father's sister. His uncle is married to her. His cousins are the children of his aunt and uncle.
notes.zh: 汤姆的姑姑是他父亲的姐妹，他的姑父娶了她，他的表兄妹是姑姑和姑父的孩子。

notes.en: Your parents are your mother and father.
notes.zh: parents 就是你的母亲和父亲。

notes.en: A crayon is made of wax.
notes.zh: 蜡笔是蜡做的。

notes.en: A cartoon has drawings of people or animals, not real people or animals.
notes.zh: 动画片里是人物或动物的图画，不是真人真动物。

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.zh: 他们会没事的，丽塔姑姑。

dialogue.speaker: children's mother
dialogue.en: Come on kids. Time to go. Thanks, Tom.
dialogue.zh: 来吧孩子们，该走了。谢谢你，汤姆。

china.en: In China, grandparents often help raise grandchildren, so formal babysitting jobs are less common than in the US.
china.zh: 在中国，祖父母常帮忙带孙辈，因此正式的临时保姆工作不如美国普遍。

china.en: Chinese community playgrounds usually have swings, slides, and sandpits just like in the US.
china.zh: 中国小区里的儿童游乐场通常也有秋千、滑梯和沙坑，和美国类似。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions in the evening routine. Irregular verbs include: fall→fell, get→got, go→went, hang→hung, lie→lay, put→put, read→read, say→said, set→set. / 一般过去时描述晚间日常中已完成的动作。不规则动词包括：fall→fell、get→got、go→went、hang→hung、lie→lay、put→put、read→read、say→said、set→set。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: When it got late,...
...Jenny yawned.
She said goodnight to her parents.
She went upstairs to her room...
...and changed into her nightgown.
She hung some of her clothes up in the closet...
steps.zh: 她把一些衣服挂进衣柜……

steps.en: ...and put her dirty clothes in the laundry basket.
She brushed her teeth,...
...washed her face,...
...and used the toilet.
After turning on her bedside lamp,...
...she turned off the room light.
She pulled back the covers...
...and got into bed.
She set her alarm clock...
...and put it on her nightstand.
She read in bed for a while.
steps.zh: 她在床上看了一会儿书。

steps.en: Finally, she turned off the lamp,...
...lay down,...
...and fell asleep.

notes.en: When she set her alarm clock, she turned the alarm to the time for it to ring in the morning.
notes.zh: 她设闹钟时，把闹铃调到早上要响的时间。

notes.en: The covers are a topsheet, blanket, bedspread, and anything else that someone sleeps under.
notes.zh: covers 指床单、毯子、床罩等睡觉时盖的所有东西。

notes.en: A nightstand is also called a bedside table.
notes.zh: nightstand 也叫作 bedside table。

notes.en: A bedside lamp is next to a bed.
notes.zh: bedside lamp 就是床头灯，放在床边。

china.en: In many Chinese apartments, dirty clothes go into a washing machine, not a laundry basket; and drying happens on the balcony.
china.zh: 在很多中国公寓里，脏衣服直接进洗衣机，而不是放在洗衣篮里；衣服晾在阳台。

china.en: Chinese bedrooms usually have a bedside table with a lamp and a phone charger (instead of an alarm clock).
china.zh: 中国卧室通常也有床头柜，上面放灯和手机充电器（而不是闹钟）。

grammarNote.en: The simple future tense uses "will" (contracted as 'll) or "be going to" to describe actions that will happen later. This unit describes a laundry plan. / 一般将来时用 will（缩略为 'll）或 be going to 描述稍后要做的动作。本单元描述一个洗衣计划。
grammarNote.zh: 一般将来时

steps.en: Later today, I'm going to do my laundry.
steps.zh: 今天晚些时候，我要洗衣服。

steps.en: I'll carry the laundry basket to the laundry room.
steps.zh: 我把洗衣篮拿到洗衣房。

steps.en: I'll take the laundry out of the basket...
steps.zh: 我把衣服从篮子里拿出来……

steps.en: ...and then I'll sort it by separating dark colors from light.
steps.zh: 然后把深色和浅色分开。

steps.en: I'll check the pockets of the pants and shirts...
steps.zh: 我检查裤子和衬衫的口袋……

steps.en: ...and take out anything I find in them.
steps.zh: 把里面发现的东西都拿出来。

steps.en: Then I'll put a load of laundry into the washing machine.
steps.zh: 然后把要洗的一批衣服放进洗衣机。

steps.en: I'll adjust the settings on the machine.
Then I'll put in some detergent...
steps.zh: 然后放一些洗衣液/洗衣粉……

steps.en: ...and turn the machine on.
The machine will wash,...
...rinse,...
...and spin the laundry.
I'll take the wet clothes out of the machine.
steps.zh: 我把湿衣服从洗衣机里拿出来。

steps.en: I'll hang some of the laundry out to dry.
steps.zh: 我把一些衣服挂出去晾干。

steps.en: I'll put some other laundry into the dryer.
steps.zh: 我把另一些放进烘干机。

steps.en: The dryer will dry it by heating and tumbling it.
steps.zh: 烘干机通过加热和翻滚来烘干衣服。

steps.en: Then I'll take it out of the machine.
steps.zh: 然后把它从烘干机里拿出来。

steps.en: I'll fold some of the dry laundry...
...and put it into drawers.
I'll iron other things...
...and hang them up in the closet.

notes.en: A load of laundry is the amount you do at one time.
notes.zh: a load of laundry 指一次洗的衣服量。

notes.en: laundry = a bunch of clothes to be (or being) washed.
notes.zh: laundry 指要洗（或正在洗）的一堆衣服。

notes.en: To sort something is to divide it into different groups.
notes.zh: sort 就是把东西分成不同的组。

notes.en: A dryer tumbles clothes by turning them over and over many times.
notes.zh: 烘干机通过反复翻滚来烘干衣服。

china.en: In China, most apartments have fully automatic washing machines, and many people use laundry pods or liquid detergent instead of powder.
china.zh: 在中国，大多数公寓有全自动洗衣机，很多人用洗衣凝珠或洗衣液而不是洗衣粉。

china.en: Electric dryers are less common; many Chinese families hang clothes on balcony racks to dry naturally in the sun.
china.zh: 烘干机不太常见，很多中国家庭把衣服挂在阳台晾衣架上自然晒干。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes habits, routines, and general facts. Here Pam and Dan regularly clean different rooms of the house. / 一般现在时描述习惯、日常和一般事实。这里帕姆和丹定期打扫家里不同的房间。
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时

steps.en: Pam picks up things that are lying around.
steps.zh: 帕姆把散落的东西收拾起来。

steps.en: She dusts the furniture...
...and the woodwork.
Then she vacuums the carpet.
steps.zh: 然后她用吸尘器吸地毯。

steps.en: Dan cleans the refrigerator...
...and throws out spoiled food.
Pam wipes the countertops...
...and sweeps the floor.
Dan scrubs the toilet with a toilet brush,...
...cleans the sink...
...and scrubs the bathtub.
He washes the mirror on the medicine cabinet.
Then he sweeps the floor...
...and mops it.
They bundle old newspapers...
...and put empty bottles, cans and jars into bags.
steps.zh: 把空瓶子、易拉罐和玻璃罐装进袋子。

steps.en: They set them out for recycling.
steps.zh: 他们把它们摆出去等回收。

steps.en: Then they empty wastebaskets...
...and the kitchen garbage into a big garbage bag...
steps.zh: 把厨房垃圾倒进大垃圾袋……

steps.en: ...and take it out to the garbage can.
steps.zh: 然后拿到外面的垃圾桶。

notes.en: When you dust furniture, you remove dust from it. Dust is a very light kind of dirt that makes a thin layer on furniture.
notes.zh: 给家具掸灰时，你把上面的灰尘擦掉。灰尘是很轻的污垢，会在家具上形成薄薄一层。

china.en: In China, many families use robot vacuum cleaners (e.g., Ecovacs, Roborock) to clean floors automatically instead of a manual vacuum.
china.zh: 在中国，很多家庭使用扫地机器人（如科沃斯、石头）自动扫地，而不用手动吸尘器。

china.en: Chinese cities like Beijing and Shanghai require mandatory garbage sorting: kitchen waste, recyclables, hazardous waste, and residual waste go in separate bins.
china.zh: 北京、上海等中国城市实行强制垃圾分类：厨余、可回收物、有害垃圾和其他垃圾分别投放。

china.en: Many Chinese apartments don't have a full bathtub; the bathroom usually has just a shower and a toilet.
china.zh: 很多中国公寓没有完整的浴缸，浴室通常只有淋浴和马桶。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions of caring for a cat. Irregular verbs: feed→fed, put→put, take→took. / 一般过去时描述照顾猫的一系列已完成动作。不规则动词：feed→fed、put→put、take→took。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: To feed his cat, Tom opened a can of cat food...
steps.zh: 为了喂猫，汤姆打开一罐猫罐头……

steps.en: ...and put it in the cat's dish.
He put some fresh water in the water dish.
steps.zh: 他在水碗里放了新鲜的水。

steps.en: He also cleaned the litter box.
He petted the cat...
...and she purred and rubbed against his leg.
steps.zh: 猫发出呼噜声，蹭他的腿。

steps.en: He played with the cat by moving a piece of string...
steps.zh: 他晃动一根绳子和猫玩……

steps.en: ...which the cat pounced on.

notes.en: A litter box is where a cat "goes to the bathroom."
notes.zh: 猫砂盆就是猫"上厕所"的地方。

notes.en: When a cat pounces, it jumps quickly on something.
notes.zh: 猫扑（pounce）就是快速跳向某物。

notes.en: Most people call their own cats "he" or "she," not "it."
notes.zh: 大多数人用 he 或 she 称呼自己的猫，而不用 it。

notes.en: The noise a cat usually makes is "meowing." When a cat is calm and happy, it "purrs." When a cat is fighting, it might "hiss."
notes.zh: 猫平时的叫声是 meow（喵），平静开心时会 purr（呼噜），打架时可能会 hiss（嘶嘶叫）。

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: Come on Kitty, get the string.

china.en: In China, cats are very popular pets in city apartments; litter boxes are used indoors, and owners buy canned cat food and dry kibble.
china.zh: 在中国，猫是城市公寓里非常受欢迎的宠物；猫砂盆在室内使用，主人买猫罐头和猫粮。

china.en: Chinese cat owners often share cute cat videos on Douyin and Xiaohongshu.
china.zh: 中国的猫主人常在抖音和小红书上分享可爱的猫咪视频。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions of caring for a dog. Irregular verbs: come→came, put→put, take→took, throw→threw. / 一般过去时描述照顾狗的一系列已完成动作。不规则动词：come→came、put→put、take→took、throw→threw。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: I called my dog.
After he came, I petted him.
He wagged his tail...
...and barked.
I put some dog food in his dish...
steps.zh: 我在他碗里放了些狗粮……

steps.en: ...and filled his water dish.
Later, I clipped a leash to his collar...
steps.zh: 后来，我把牵引绳扣在他项圈上……

steps.en: ...and took him out for a walk.
After his walk, I threw a stick for him...
steps.zh: 散步后，我扔了根棍子给他……

steps.en: ...and he fetched it.

notes.en: A dog's collar goes around his neck.
notes.zh: 狗的项圈戴在脖子上。

notes.en: A dog fetches something by picking it up in his mouth and taking it back to the person who threw it.
notes.zh: 狗捡东西是用嘴叼起来，带回给扔东西的人。

notes.en: Most people call their own dogs "he" or "she," not "it."
notes.zh: 大多数人用 he 或 she 称呼自己的狗，而不用 it。

notes.en: A dog wags his tail by moving it back and forth.
notes.zh: 狗摇尾巴就是来回摆动尾巴。

notes.en: Usually a dog's noise is called barking. If a dog is hurt, it "yelps" (suddenly) or "whines" (for a longer time). A dog might also "howl."
notes.zh: 狗通常的叫声叫 barking（吠）。受伤时会 yelp（突然叫）或 whine（哀鸣很久），狗还可能 howl（嚎叫）。

china.en: In China, dog owners must register their dogs with the police and keep them on a leash in public, as required by local pet regulations.
china.zh: 在中国，养犬人必须按当地规定给狗上户口，并在公共场合牵绳。

china.en: Many Chinese parks have designated dog-walking areas, and dog-waste bags are commonly provided.
china.zh: 很多中国公园有专门的遛狗区，通常会提供拾便袋。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed plant-care actions. Irregular verbs include: fill→filled, water→watered, pull→pulled, loosen→loosened, pick→picked.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时描述已完成的养花动作：filled 装满、watered 浇水、pulled 拔、loosened 松、picked 摘。

steps.en: Jenny helped Grandma water the potted plants on the balcony.
steps.zh: 珍妮帮奶奶给阳台上的盆栽浇水。

steps.en: She filled a small watering can with water.
She watered the plants.
She pulled the small weeds out of the pots.
steps.zh: 她把花盆里的小杂草拔掉。

steps.en: She loosened the soil with a small stick.
She picked a flower for Grandma.
Grandma said, "Thank you! You are a good helper."
steps.zh: 奶奶说：“谢谢你！你真是个好帮手。”

notes.en: A watering can is a small container with a spout, used to water plants.
notes.zh: watering can（喷壶）是带嘴的小容器，用来给植物浇水。

notes.en: A weed is a plant you don't want. Weeds grow between flowers and take their food.
notes.zh: weed 是你不想要的植物（杂草），它长在花中间抢养分。

notes.en: Plants need water, sunlight and good soil to grow well.
notes.zh: 植物需要水、阳光和好土壤才能长得好。

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.en: Thank you! You are a good helper.
dialogue.zh: 谢谢你！你真是个好帮手。

china.en: In Chinese cities, most families live in apartments and grow flowers in pots on the balcony; lawns are rare and maintained by property management.
china.zh: 在中国城市，多数家庭住楼房，在阳台用花盆栽花；草坪很少见，由物业统一维护。

china.en: Potted plants like pothos, lucky bamboo and mint are common choices for Chinese homes.
china.zh: 绿萝、富贵竹、薄荷等盆栽是中国家庭常见的选择。

grammarNote.en: The simple future tense uses "will" and contractions like 'll to describe actions Tom will do in his garden. / 一般将来时用 will 和缩略形式 'll 描述汤姆将在花园里做的事。
grammarNote.zh: 一般将来时

steps.en: Tom will turn the soil with a spade.
He'll plant some seeds...
...and cover them with a mound of soil.
He'll plant some seedlings...
...and tie them to small stakes.
steps.zh: 然后把它们绑在小支架上。

steps.en: Then he'll water the garden.
Tom will weed the garden.
He'll prune extra leaves from some plants.
steps.zh: 他会给一些植物剪掉多余的叶子。

steps.en: He'll check for harmful insects...
...and spray insecticide on some plants.
steps.zh: 然后给一些植物喷杀虫剂。

steps.en: He'll put some fertilizer on the soil.
steps.zh: 他会在土壤上施一些肥。

steps.en: Finally, he'll pick some flowers for the house.
steps.zh: 最后，他会摘一些花插在家里。

notes.en: A seedling is a very young plant. The ones you plant in your garden started growing somewhere else first.
notes.zh: seedling 就是很小的植物幼苗，你种到花园里的苗是先在别处长出来的。

notes.en: You weed a garden by pulling out the weeds — unwanted plants.
notes.zh: 除草就是把花园里不需要的杂草拔掉。

notes.en: Harmful insects are those that are bad for plants.
notes.zh: 害虫就是对植物有害的昆虫。

notes.en: Fertilizer adds useful chemicals to soil.
notes.zh: 肥料给土壤添加有用的化学物质。

notes.en: To check for harmful insects is to look at something for a short time trying to find the insects.
notes.zh: check for harmful insects 就是短时间查看，试图找到害虫。

china.en: In China, many urban residents grow vegetables and herbs in balcony containers rather than in a backyard garden.
china.zh: 在中国，很多城市居民在阳台花盆里种蔬菜和香草，而不是在后院花园里。

china.en: Community shared gardens are becoming popular in Chinese cities, where residents rent small plots to grow their own vegetables.
china.zh: 城市里社区共享菜园越来越流行，居民租小块地自己种蔬菜。
