grammarNote.en: The simple present tense is used here to describe a regular, habitual routine and the standard steps of a process (cleaning a car). It expresses actions that are repeated or done according to a usual procedure.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般现在时描述日常习惯和固定流程步骤（洗车的标准步骤），表示反复发生或按常规做法进行的动作。

steps.en: I wash the windows inside,...
...wipe off the dashboard...
...and vacuum the floor.
steps.zh: ……然后用吸尘器把地板吸干净。

steps.en: I dip a sponge into soapy water...
steps.zh: 我把海绵蘸进肥皂水里……

steps.en: ...and wash the car with it.
To rinse the car, I spray it with water.
steps.zh: 要冲洗汽车，我用水喷洒它。

steps.en: I dry it with some rags.
steps.zh: 我用一些抹布把它擦干。

steps.en: Then I spread some wax on the car.
steps.zh: 然后我在车上打一些车蜡。

steps.en: After it has dried,...
...I wipe the wax off...
...and buff the car with a soft cloth.
Finally, I wash the windows outside.
steps.zh: 最后，我清洗车外的车窗。

notes.en: A rag is a kind of cloth used for cleaning. Many rags come from old clothing. A sponge has a lot of holes in it. It holds water and can be squeezed to a small size.
notes.zh: rag（抹布）是一种用来清洁的布，很多抹布是用旧衣服改的。sponge（海绵）有很多小孔，能吸水，也可以被挤压得很小。

notes.en: You buff something by moving a cloth quickly back and forth.
notes.zh: buff 是指用布快速来回擦拭，把东西擦亮。

notes.en: You spray a car with a widely-spread stream of water.
notes.zh: spray 是用一束散开的水流喷洒汽车。

notes.en: Wax makes a car shine.
notes.zh: wax（车蜡）能让汽车发亮。

notes.en: You rinse a car to remove soapy water.
notes.zh: rinse（冲洗）是为了把车上的肥皂水冲掉。

china.en: In China, many car owners drive to a car wash shop or gas station to have their cars washed; self-service home washing is less common in cities.
china.zh: 在中国，车主多开车去洗车店或加油站洗车，城市里自己在家洗车的情况较少。

china.en: Chinese car owners often get a free car wash as part of regular maintenance at a 4S dealership.
china.zh: 中国车主去4S店做保养时，常常会获赠一次免费洗车。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense is used here to narrate a completed sequence of past events: calling for an appointment, taking the car to the garage, getting an estimate, and picking it up later.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般过去时叙述一连串已经发生的事情：打电话预约、把车送修、拿到估价，以及之后取车。

steps.en: I called for an appointment to get my car fixed.
I took my car in to the garage...
...and the mechanic diagnosed the problem.
I asked him for an estimate of the cost.
steps.zh: 我请他给出维修费用的估价。

steps.en: He worked on the engine.
When I came back later to pick up the car,...
...he gave me the bill for the repair.

verbs.zh: v. 得到，使（过去式 got）
v. 带走，送去（过去式 took）

notes.en: for repairs = for actions that correct problems.
notes.zh: for repairs 意思是“为了纠正问题所做的维修行动”。

notes.en: When you get something fixed, you arrange for someone else to fix it. You don't fix it yourself.
notes.zh: get something fixed 是指安排别人来修，而不是自己动手修。

notes.en: To diagnose a problem is to figure out what it is by noticing what has caused it. A doctor diagnoses illnesses.
notes.zh: diagnose（诊断）是通过观察原因来弄清楚问题出在哪里；医生诊断疾病用的就是这个词。

notes.en: An estimate is a guess about an amount (of money, time, etc.).
notes.zh: estimate（估价）是对金额、时间等的大致估计。

notes.en: To call for an appointment is to telephone someone and set up a time when you can meet.
notes.zh: call for an appointment 是打电话给对方，约定一个见面时间。

notes.en: "Ouch" is something people say when they've been hurt.
notes.zh: Ouch（哎哟）是人们受伤或感到疼痛时发出的叫声。

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: My car is making a strange noise. When can you look at it?
dialogue.zh: 我的车发出奇怪的声音。你什么时候能来看一下？

dialogue.speaker: Mechanic
dialogue.en: Yep. Sounds like a valve problem.
dialogue.zh: 嗯。听起来像是气门的问题。

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: How much will it cost to fix?

dialogue.speaker: Mechanic
dialogue.en: That'll be two ninety-four for parts and labor.
dialogue.zh: 零件和工时费一共两百九十四。

china.en: In China, drivers usually book repairs through 4S shops or WeChat, and pay by mobile payment when picking up the car.
china.zh: 在中国，车主通常通过4S店或微信预约修车，取车时用手机支付结账。

china.en: Many Chinese car brands offer free roadside assistance and even door-to-door pick-up and delivery service.
china.zh: 很多中国汽车品牌提供免费道路救援，甚至上门取送车服务。

units.en: Taking a Car to a Garage for Repairs

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense tells the story of one specific occasion: the car got a flat tire and the speaker changed it step by step.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般过去时讲述一次具体经历：车胎瘪了，说话人一步步把备胎换上。

steps.en: My car had a flat tire, so I had to change it.
steps.zh: 我的车胎瘪了，所以我得换备胎。

steps.en: I jacked the car up.
steps.zh: 我用千斤顶把车顶起来。

steps.en: I took off the flat tire...
steps.zh: 我把瘪了的轮胎卸下来……

steps.en: ...and took the spare tire out of the trunk.
I put the spare on the wheel,...
...tightened the lug nuts by hand...
...lowered the car to the ground,...
...and tightened the nuts some more with a lug wrench.
steps.zh: ……然后用轮胎扳手再把螺母拧紧一些。

steps.en: Finally, I put the hubcap on the wheel.
steps.zh: 最后，我把轮毂盖装回轮子上。

verbs.zh: v. 装上，放上（过去式同形 put）
v. 拆下，卸下（过去式 took）

notes.en: A spare thing is extra—something you don't usually need.
notes.zh: spare 表示“额外的、备用的”，也就是平时用不到、临时才拿出来用的东西。

notes.en: You can jack something up but you cannot "jack it down." Instead, you lower it.
notes.zh: 可以说 jack something up（用千斤顶顶起），但不能说 jack it down；要“放下”用 lower。

notes.en: To the ground means to the surface of the earth.
notes.zh: to the ground 意思是“落到地面上”。

notes.en: A nut goes on a bolt. (See p. 61.)
notes.zh: nut（螺母）是拧在 bolt（螺栓）上的。（见第61页。）

china.en: In China, most drivers call roadside assistance (122 traffic police or the insurance hotline) rather than changing a tire themselves on the highway.
china.zh: 在中国，大部分司机在高速上爆胎会打122或保险救援电话，而不是自己动手换胎。

china.en: Many new Chinese cars are equipped with tire pressure monitors and repair kits; some use run-flat tires and no longer carry a full-size spare.
china.zh: 很多国产新车配有胎压监测和补胎工具，部分车使用缺气保用胎，不再配备全尺寸备胎。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense narrates a one-time event: a thunderstorm caused a power outage, and the family responded step by step until the power came back.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般过去时叙述一次具体事件：雷雨导致停电，一家人一步步应对，直到恢复供电。

steps.en: During a thunderstorm...
...our power went out.
I turned on a flashlight...
...and my sister lit some candles.
We found the circuit-breaker box...
...and found the breakers that had tripped.
We reset the breakers...
...and the power came back on.

verbs.zh: v. （电）恢复，到来（过去式 came）
v. 应对，处理（过去式 dealt）

notes.en: Here, power means "electric power."
notes.zh: 这里的 power 指“电力”。

notes.en: Circuit breakers look like switches. They trip—switch off—if too much electric power hits them.
notes.zh: 断路器看起来像开关。电流过大时它会跳闸（自动断开）。

notes.en: Some houses have fuses instead of circuit breakers.
notes.zh: 有些老房子用保险丝（fuse），而不是断路器。

notes.en: Breaker is a short form of "circuit-breaker."
notes.zh: breaker 是 circuit-breaker 的简称。

notes.en: In a thunderstorm, there are bright flashes of light called lightning. The sound that follows lightning is called "thunder."
notes.zh: 雷暴雨时，天上明亮的闪光叫 lightning（闪电），随后听到的响声叫 thunder（雷）。

notes.en: To deal with a power failure is to do the right things after one happens.
notes.zh: deal with a power failure 就是停电发生后采取正确的应对措施。

china.en: In Chinese cities, scheduled power outages are usually announced in advance by the grid company; unexpected outages are relatively rare.
china.zh: 在中国城市，计划停电一般会由电网公司提前通知，突发停电相对少见。

china.en: Chinese people often use their phones as flashlights during a blackout and keep power banks charged for emergencies.
china.zh: 停电时中国人常用手机当手电筒，并平时备好充电宝应急。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes general, repeatable instructions and facts about how to work with wood.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般现在时讲解木工活的通用步骤和常识，表示可重复操作的做法。

steps.en: Before you cut a board, you measure it...
steps.zh: 锯木板之前，你先量一下尺寸……

steps.en: ...and mark the places to cut.
Then you cut it with a saw.
To trim a piece of wood, you plane it.
steps.zh: 要修整一块木料，你用刨子刨平。

steps.en: To make the edges smooth, you sand them.
steps.zh: 要把边缘磨光滑，你用砂纸打磨。

steps.en: To join two pieces of wood, you can glue them together,...
steps.zh: 要把两块木料接起来，你可以用胶水粘……

steps.en: ...nail them together,...
...or join them with screws.

notes.en: A board is a wide, flat piece of wood.
notes.zh: board 指一块又宽又平的木板。

notes.en: You pound a nail with a hammer.
notes.zh: 用锤子把钉子敲进去。

notes.en: Some things you can measure a board with: ruler (rule) — usually 12 inches long; yardstick — 1 yard (36 inches) long; tape measure — can measure longer distances.
notes.zh: 可以用来量木板的工具：ruler（直尺）通常12英寸长；yardstick（码尺）长1码（36英寸）；tape measure（卷尺）可以量更长的距离。

notes.en: To join things is to put them together.
notes.zh: join 意思是把东西拼到一起。

notes.en: You glue things together with glue, nail them together with nails, and screw them together with screws.
notes.zh: 用胶水粘是 glue together，用钉子钉是 nail together，用螺丝固定是 screw together。

china.en: In Chinese cities, home repairs are usually done by a hired handyman or the property management; few households keep a full woodworking tool set.
china.zh: 在中国城市，家里修修补补一般找师傅或物业，很少家庭自备全套木工工具。

china.en: Chinese hardware stores (wujin dian) sell affordable hand tools, and many people buy flat-pack furniture from IKEA-style stores and assemble it themselves.
china.zh: 中国的五金店工具便宜，很多人买宜家式的拼装家具自己动手组装。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense gives general, step-by-step instructions for fastening things with bolts and screws.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般现在时讲解用螺栓和螺丝紧固东西的通用步骤。

steps.en: You put a bolt through some holes...
...put a washer onto the bolt...
...and then tighten a nut by hand.
Then you hold the nut with a pair of pliers...
steps.zh: 然后你用一把钳子夹住螺母……

steps.en: ...and tighten the bolt with a wrench.
You drill a hole for the screw.
You put a screwdriver into the slot on the head of the screw.
steps.zh: 你把螺丝刀插进螺丝头的槽里。

steps.en: You tighten the screw by turning the screwdriver clockwise.
steps.zh: 顺时针转动螺丝刀把螺丝拧紧。

steps.en: To loosen the screw, you turn it counter-clockwise.
steps.zh: 要拧松螺丝，就逆时针转动。

notes.en: It's always pliers—with an "s."
notes.zh: pliers 这个词总是带 s，是复数形式（一把钳子也要说 a pair of pliers）。

notes.en: Clockwise means "in the same direction as the hands of a clock move."
notes.zh: clockwise 意思是“和钟表指针转动方向相同”，即顺时针。

notes.en: Counter-clockwise is the opposite.
notes.zh: counter-clockwise 意思正好相反，即逆时针。

notes.en: You drill holes with a drill. You bolt things together with bolts and screw them together with screws.
notes.zh: 用 drill（电钻）钻孔；用 bolts（螺栓）把东西 bolt together；用 screws（螺丝）把东西 screw together。

china.en: In China, battery-powered screwdrivers and affordable electric drills are popular online (Taobao/JD) for self-assembly furniture.
china.zh: 在中国，充电式螺丝刀和便宜的电钻在淘宝、京东上很畅销，多用于拼装家具。

china.en: Chinese DIY culture is growing; many young people mount shelves, TVs and curtain rods themselves.
china.zh: 中国的 DIY 文化越来越流行，很多年轻人自己装置物架、电视和窗帘杆。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes Tom's regular routine of grocery shopping from start to finish.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般现在时描述汤姆一贯的买菜购物流程，从进超市到结账。

steps.en: Tom gets a shopping cart.
Some people use a basket instead of a cart.
steps.zh: 有些人用购物篮而不用购物车。

steps.en: He checks his shopping list to see what he should buy.
steps.zh: 他对照购物清单看自己该买什么。

steps.en: In the fresh produce section, he checks the fruit and vegetables by feeling...
steps.zh: 在生鲜区，他通过摸……来挑选蔬菜水果……

steps.en: ...and smelling them.
He puts some fruit in a plastic bag...
steps.zh: 他把一些水果装进塑料袋……

steps.en: ...and weighs the fruit on a scale.
Next, he picks up some fresh meat at the meat counter.
steps.zh: 接着，他在肉类柜台买了一些鲜肉。

steps.en: Then, at the deli, he gets some cold cuts...
steps.zh: 然后在熟食柜台，他买了一些冷切肉……

steps.en: ...and cheese.
He goes through the canned goods aisle.
steps.zh: 他走过罐装食品货架通道。

steps.en: He checks the prices on two brands of canned peas...
steps.zh: 他比较两个品牌罐装豌豆的价格……

steps.en: ...and chooses the cheaper one.
As he shops, he looks for specials.
steps.zh: 购物时，他留意特价商品。

steps.en: He picks up some toilet paper in the household goods section...
steps.zh: 他在家居用品区拿了一些卫生纸……

steps.en: ...and gets some milk in the dairy section.
steps.zh: ……然后在乳制品区买了一些牛奶。

steps.en: He tries a free sample of some pizza...
steps.zh: 他试吃了一份免费的披萨样品……

steps.en: ...and takes some frozen pizza from the frozen-food case.
steps.zh: ……然后从冷冻柜里拿了一些冷冻披萨。

steps.en: Finally, he goes to the checkout counter.

notes.en: A section is a part of something—here it's part of a store.
notes.zh: section 指某物的一部分，这里指超市里的一个区域。

notes.en: Cold cuts are already cooked meats that you eat cold in a sandwich.
notes.zh: cold cuts 是已经做熟的冷切肉，可以夹在三明治里冷吃。

notes.en: Tom checks his list—looks quickly at it to see what it says.
notes.zh: check his list 是指快速看一眼清单，确认要买什么。

notes.en: Tom checks the fruit—looks at it, smells it, and feels it quickly to see if it's good.
notes.zh: check the fruit 是指看一看、闻一闻、摸一摸，快速判断水果新不新鲜。

notes.en: Something that is on special is at a lower price than usual. This lower price is called a special.
notes.zh: on special 表示比平时便宜；这种特价商品本身也叫 special。

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: I'll have four chicken breasts, please.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: Some beef pastrami, please. Six slices.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: And a half pound of cheddar.

dialogue.speaker: Promoter
dialogue.en: Try some, sir? It's on special!

china.en: In China, many people buy groceries on apps like Hema (Freshippo) or Meituan, and goods are delivered to the door in about 30 minutes.
china.zh: 在中国，很多人用盒马、美团等 App 买菜，大约30分钟送货上门。

china.en: Chinese supermarkets have self-checkout lanes where you scan items and pay by QR code; plastic bags are charged separately.
china.zh: 中国超市普遍有自助结账机，扫商品后扫码支付；塑料袋需要单独付费。

china.en: Traditional wet markets (caishichang) are still popular; vendors weigh, bag and even bargain for you.
china.zh: 传统菜市场仍然很常见，摊贩会帮你称重、装袋，还可以讲价。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes the standard, repeated procedure of paying in a store—with cash or by scanning a payment code with the phone.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般现在时描述在商店付款的两种常见流程：现金和手机扫码支付。

steps.en: The cashier rings up Tom's purchases...
steps.zh: 收银员把汤姆买的东西扫码录入……

steps.en: ...by scanning the bar codes...
...and pressing keys on the cash register.
She tells him the total to pay.
steps.zh: 她告诉他应付的总金额。

steps.en: Tom takes out his wallet, gives her the money...
steps.zh: 汤姆拿出钱包，把钱递给她……

steps.en: ...and she gives him his change.
Then Tom takes out his phone and shows the payment code.
steps.zh: 然后汤姆拿出手机，出示付款码。

steps.en: The cashier scans the code with her scanner...
steps.zh: 收银员用扫码器扫他的付款码……

steps.en: ...and gives him a receipt.

notes.en: To ring something up means to make a machine record its price.
notes.zh: ring something up 意思是用收银机把商品价格录入并计算总额。

notes.en: The money I give the cashier is more than the total price. The difference is my change.
notes.zh: 我付给收银员的钱比应付总额多，多出来的部分就是找零（change）。

notes.en: In China, people usually pay by showing a payment code on the phone; the cashier scans it.
notes.zh: 在中国，大家通常出示手机付款码，收银员扫一下就能完成支付。

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.en: Here's your change and your receipt.

china.en: In China, WeChat Pay and Alipay dominate; showing a payment code or scanning the merchant's code is the norm, even at small shops.
china.zh: 在中国，微信支付和支付宝无处不在；出示付款码或扫商家二维码是主流，小店也一样。

china.en: The cashier often says the amount aloud, and the phone says "Payment received" (收款 X 元).
china.zh: 收银员常会报出金额，手机也会语音提示“收款 X 元”。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense narrates one trip to the bank with Dad: took a number, waited, went to the counter, gave the ID card, checked, got the money and a receipt.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般过去时讲述和爸爸去银行办业务的一次经历：取号、等待、去柜台、递身份证、核对、拿到钱和回执。

steps.en: Tom went to the bank with his dad.
He took a number ticket from the machine.
steps.zh: 他在取号机上取了一张号。

steps.en: They waited in the waiting area.
When the screen showed their number, they went to the counter.
steps.zh: 屏幕显示他们的号时，他们走到柜台。

steps.en: Dad gave the teller his ID card.
steps.zh: 爸爸把身份证递给柜员。

steps.en: The teller checked the information on the computer.
steps.zh: 柜员在电脑上核对信息。

steps.en: She gave Dad the money and a receipt.
steps.zh: 她把钱和回执交给爸爸。

steps.en: Tom helped Dad count the money.

notes.en: A number ticket tells you your turn. The screen calls your number, then you go to the counter.
notes.zh: 排队号告诉你轮到你没有，屏幕叫号后你再去柜台。

notes.en: A teller is a bank worker who helps people do business at the counter.
notes.zh: teller（柜员）是在柜台帮客户办理业务的银行工作人员。

notes.en: Many people in China do banking on their phones, so banks are not very busy now.
notes.zh: 现在很多中国人用手机银行办业务，银行柜台不太忙了。

china.en: In Chinese banks, you take a number ticket, wait in the waiting area, and watch the screen for your number.
china.zh: 在中国银行，你要取号、在等候区等待、看屏幕叫号。

china.en: Chinese banks use ID cards and electronic records instead of passbooks; kids usually go with parents for big money or new cards.
china.zh: 中国银行用身份证和电子记录，不用存折；孩子通常是陪家长去办大额业务或开新卡。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense tells the story of Kate's trip to an ATM to withdraw cash.
grammarNote.zh: 这里用一般过去时讲述凯特去自动取款机取钱的经历。

steps.en: Kate needed money...
...so she went to an ATM in the store.
steps.zh: ……于是她去了商店里的一台自动取款机。

steps.en: She took her cash card out of her purse.
steps.zh: 她从钱包里取出银行卡。

steps.en: She lined up the magnetic strip properly...
...and inserted the card into the slot on the ATM.
A message on the screen asked for her PIN...
steps.zh: 屏幕上的信息提示她输入密码……

steps.en: ...so she entered her PIN by pressing keys on the keypad.
steps.zh: ……于是她在键盘上输入了密码。

steps.en: Then she entered the amount of money she needed.
steps.zh: 然后她输入了需要取的金额。

steps.en: The machine returned her card...
...and gave her her money.

notes.en: An ATM is an Automated Teller Machine. Another name for it is "cash machine."
notes.zh: ATM 是 Automated Teller Machine（自动柜员机）的缩写，也叫 cash machine。

notes.en: Cash is money in the form of notes and coins (not checks).
notes.zh: cash 指纸币和硬币形式的现金，不包括支票。

notes.en: A PIN is a Personal Identification Number.
notes.zh: PIN 是 Personal Identification Number 的缩写，即个人密码。

notes.en: You enter a number by typing it into a machine or writing it on a form.
notes.zh: enter a number 是指在机器上键入数字，或在表格上写下数字。

notes.en: Insert something into means "put something in." You insert something into an opening (a hole, a slot, etc.).
notes.zh: insert something into 意思是“把某物放进去”，即把它插进一个开口（洞、插槽等）里。

dialogue.speaker: Kate
dialogue.en: Oops. I'd better find a cash machine.
dialogue.zh: 哎呀，我最好找台取款机。

china.en: In China, ATMs are used less and less; people rely on mobile payment and rarely carry cash.
china.zh: 在中国，ATM 使用频率越来越低；大家主要靠手机支付，很少带现金。

china.en: Chinese ATMs accept UnionPay cards; many newer ones support facial recognition and cardless withdrawals via mobile banking.
china.zh: 中国的ATM支持银联卡，很多新机支持刷脸和手机银行无卡取款。

china.en: Small convenience stores even offer "cash-back" services where you can withdraw small amounts when paying.
china.zh: 一些便利店还提供小额取现服务，付款时可以顺便取现金。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense describes completed actions that happened in the past. Regular verbs add -ed (dialed, answered), but many common verbs are irregular (hear→heard, ring→rang, say→said, make→made).
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时用来描述过去发生并已完成的动作。规则动词加 -ed（如 dialed、answered），但很多常见动词是不规则的（如 hear→heard、ring→rang、say→said、make→made）。

steps.en: Jenny looked up Kate's phone number in the phone book.
steps.zh: 珍妮在电话簿里查了凯特的电话号码。

steps.en: She picked up the receiver...
...and heard a dial tone.
Then she dialed the number.
She heard Kate's phone ringing.
steps.zh: 她听到凯特的电话在响。

steps.en: When Kate answered...
...Jenny said hello and identified herself.
steps.zh: ……珍妮打了招呼并报上了自己的名字。

steps.en: Then she said why she called.
steps.zh: 然后她说明了打电话的原因。

notes.en: Phone is a short way of saying "telephone."
notes.zh: phone 是 telephone（电话）的简略说法。

notes.en: Receiver means the part of the telephone that you put near your ear and mouth.
notes.zh: receiver（听筒）指电话上贴近耳朵和嘴的那部分。

notes.en: Most modern telephones are push-button phones — you dial by pushing buttons.
notes.zh: 大多数现代电话是按键式电话——你通过按按钮来拨号。

notes.en: A dial tone is a sound that tells you the phone is ready to use. If you pick up the receiver and you don't hear one, the phone might be "dead" — not working.
notes.zh: 拨号音是提示你电话可以使用的声音。如果拿起听筒却听不到拨号音，电话可能“坏了”——无法使用。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: I'm calling to see whether you'd like to go swimming.
dialogue.zh: 我打电话来是想问你想不想去游泳。

china.en: In China, people rarely use traditional landline phones; most people call directly on mobile phones.
china.zh: 在中国，人们很少使用传统座机，大多直接用手机打电话。

china.en: WeChat voice and video calls are very popular and often replace regular phone calls.
china.zh: 微信语音和视频通话非常流行，常常取代普通电话。

china.en: Phone numbers are saved in contacts, so people no longer need a phone book.
china.zh: 号码都存在手机通讯录里，人们不再需要电话簿。

grammarNote.en: This unit continues the simple past with irregular forms like hear→heard, hang→hung, speak→spoke, tell→told, know→knew, as the story describes a completed phone call.
grammarNote.zh: 本单元继续使用一般过去时，通过 hear→heard、hang→hung、speak→spoke、tell→told、know→knew 等不规则过去式，叙述一次已完成的通话。

steps.en: Kate heard the phone ringing...
...and picked up the receiver.
She answered the phone by saying hello...
...and then let the caller speak.
They talked for a while,...
...and then she hung up.
Kate didn't know the person the caller asked for.
steps.zh: 凯特不认识来电者要找的人。

steps.en: She told him that he had the wrong number.
He apologized and hung up.
steps.zh: 他道了歉然后挂了电话。

notes.en: To let someone speak you stay silent.
notes.zh: 让对方说话时，你保持沉默。

notes.en: The person who answers a phone usually speaks first.
notes.zh: 接电话的人通常先开口说话。

notes.en: The caller usually says goodbye first.
notes.zh: 打电话的人通常先说再见。

dialogue.speaker: Kate
dialogue.zh: 我很想去，珍妮。什么时候？

dialogue.speaker: Kate
dialogue.en: I'm sorry. There's no one here by that name. You've got the wrong number.
dialogue.zh: 抱歉，这里没有叫这个名字的人。你打错了。

china.en: Wrong numbers are rare in China because people save contacts and redial from them.
china.zh: 在中国，打错电话的情况很少，因为人们都保存联系人并直接回拨。

china.en: People often use speakerphone or Bluetooth earphones to talk while doing other things.
china.zh: 人们常常在做事时用免提或蓝牙耳机通话。

china.en: Missed calls are usually returned with a WeChat message rather than a phone callback.
china.zh: 未接来电通常通过微信消息回复，而不是回拨电话。

grammarNote.en: The simple past describes a completed phone interaction: asked, wasn't, identified, agreed, repeated, left, asked. Note the irregular verbs leave→left, speak→spoke, take→took.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时描述一次已完成的通话：asked、wasn't、identified、agreed、repeated、left、asked。注意不规则动词 leave→left、speak→spoke、take→took。

steps.en: I asked to speak to Dan...
...but he wasn't available.
I identified myself and asked her to take a message.
steps.zh: 我报上姓名，请她捎个口信。

steps.en: She agreed and asked me to repeat my name.
steps.zh: 她答应了，并让我重复一遍名字。

steps.en: I repeated it...
...and spelled my last name.
I also left my number...
...and asked that he call me back.

notes.en: Someone who is available is able to see you or speak with you. If he is not available, he may be somewhere else or too busy to speak to you.
notes.zh: available 指某人能见你或能和你说话。如果他 not available，可能是不在或太忙没空接你。

notes.en: When you leave your message, you tell it to whoever is taking the message.
notes.zh: 当你留言时，你把话告诉那个帮你捎口信的人。

notes.en: To repeat something is to say it again.
notes.zh: repeat 就是把话再说一遍。

notes.en: Alex Rivera's first name is "Alex." His last name is "Rivera." For most people of European descent, the last name is a family name. It is also called a "surname."
notes.zh: 亚历克斯·里维拉的名是 Alex，姓是 Rivera。对大多数欧洲血统的人来说，姓就是家族姓氏，也叫 surname。

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: Can I speak to Dan, please?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.en: I'm sorry, but he's not here right now.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: This is Alex. I work with Dan. Could you please take a message for him?
dialogue.zh: 我是亚历克斯，和丹一起工作。能麻烦你帮我捎个口信给他吗？

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.en: Sure. I'm sorry. I didn't catch your name.
dialogue.zh: 好的。抱歉，我没听清你的名字。

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.zh: 我是亚历克斯，亚历克斯·里维拉。

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.en: Could you spell that out, please?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: Could you ask him to give me a call, please? Thanks.
dialogue.zh: 能请他给我回个电话吗？谢谢。

china.en: In China, if someone can't answer, people usually leave a WeChat voice or text message instead of asking a third person to take a message.
china.zh: 在中国，如果对方不方便接听，人们通常直接发微信语音或文字留言，而不是请第三人捎口信。

china.en: Business contacts often use call-back on the phone or simply send a WeChat message.
china.zh: 商务联系常用手机回拨功能，或直接在微信上发消息。

china.en: There is no need to spell out names because contacts are saved with notes and numbers are dialed automatically.
china.zh: 不需要拼写名字，因为联系人都存了备注，号码自动拨出。

grammarNote.en: The past tense narrates the sequence: answered, asked, said, offered, left, wrote, put, got, returned. Irregular forms include leave→left, take→took, write→wrote, put→put.
grammarNote.zh: 过去时按顺序叙述：answered、asked、said、offered、left、wrote、put、got、returned。不规则形式有 leave→left、take→took、write→wrote、put→put。

steps.en: Pam answered the phone...
...and the caller asked for Dan.
She said he wasn't available and offered to take a message.
steps.zh: 她说他没空，并主动提出可以捎口信。

steps.en: The caller left a message for Dan.
Pam wrote the message on some notepaper...
steps.zh: 帕姆把留言写在便签纸上……

steps.en: ...and put it next to the phone.
Later, Dan got the message...
...and returned Lester's call.

notes.en: Pam says "He can't come to the phone." This is a way of not giving too much information about Dan.
notes.zh: 帕姆说“He can't come to the phone”（他没法来接电话），这是一种不透露丹太多信息的委婉说法。

notes.en: The caller left a message for Dan with Pam.
notes.zh: 来电者通过帕姆给丹留了言。

notes.en: Notepaper is usually small, especially for taking short messages. Many sheets of notepaper joined together make a notepad.
notes.zh: 便签纸通常很小，尤其用来记短留言。许多张便签纸订在一起就是一个便签本。

notes.en: If you return a call, you call back someone who left a message for you.
notes.zh: 回电话就是给给你留言的人回拨过去。

notes.en: Pam offered to take a message by saying, "Can I take a message?" Other ways to say this are: "Would you like to leave a message?" and "Is there any message?"
notes.zh: 帕姆通过说“Can I take a message?”主动提出捎口信。其他说法有：“Would you like to leave a message?”和“Is there any message?”

dialogue.speaker: Pam
dialogue.en: Sorry. He can't come to the phone right now. Can I take a message?
dialogue.zh: 抱歉，他现在没法来接电话。需要我捎个口信吗？

dialogue.speaker: Lester
dialogue.en: Yes, please tell him that Lester called.
dialogue.zh: 好的，请告诉他莱斯特来过电话。

dialogue.speaker: Dan
dialogue.en: Hi, Lester. This is Dan. You called?
dialogue.zh: 嗨，莱斯特。我是丹。你找我？

china.en: In China, people rarely write phone messages on paper; they send text or WeChat messages directly.
china.zh: 在中国，人们很少用纸写电话留言，而是直接发短信或微信。

china.en: Missed calls show the caller's name and number on the phone screen, so no written message is needed.
china.zh: 未接来电会在手机屏幕上显示来电者姓名和号码，无需书面留言。

china.en: Smartphones can transcribe voicemail to text automatically.
china.zh: 智能手机可以自动把语音信箱转成文字。

grammarNote.en: The past tense tells a complete story of voice messages: recorded, heard, left, got home, saw, tapped, played, listened, took, deleted. Irregular verbs: get→got, hear→heard, leave→left, see→saw, take→took.
grammarNote.zh: 过去时完整讲述语音留言的过程：recorded、heard、left、got home、saw、tapped、played、listened、took、deleted。不规则动词：get→got、hear→heard、leave→left、see→saw、take→took。

steps.en: Tom recorded a voice message on his phone.
steps.zh: 汤姆在手机上录了一段语音留言。

steps.en: When Jenny called him, she heard the message...
steps.zh: 珍妮打电话给他时，听到了这段留言……

steps.en: ...and left her own voice message for him.
steps.zh: ……并给他留了自己的语音留言。

steps.en: When Tom got home, he saw a red dot on his phone.
steps.zh: 汤姆回家时，看到手机上有红点。

steps.en: He tapped the message to play it.
As he listened to it, he took some notes.
steps.zh: 他听留言时，记了一些笔记。

steps.en: Then he deleted the message.

notes.en: When you record a voice message, you put it on the phone. When you delete it, you take it off.
notes.zh: 录制语音留言就是把它存进手机，删除就是把它清掉。

notes.en: In WeChat, a red dot shows that a new voice message is waiting for you.
notes.zh: 在微信里，红点提示你有新的语音留言等着听。

notes.en: A voice message can be played again and again, and it is saved automatically.
notes.zh: 语音留言可以反复播放，而且会自动保存。

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: I can't answer the phone right now. Please leave a message.
dialogue.zh: 我现在不能接电话，请留言。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Tom, this is Jenny. Please call me back. Let's play basketball together!
dialogue.zh: 汤姆，我是珍妮。请给我回电话，我们一起打篮球吧！

china.en: In China, answering machines are almost gone; people leave WeChat voice messages instead.
china.zh: 在中国，答录机几乎绝迹，大家改用微信语音留言。

china.en: WeChat voice messages are saved and can be replayed anytime, so no one needs to erase them by hand.
china.zh: 微信语音会自动保存、随时重听，不需要手动删除。

grammarNote.en: The narrative uses the simple past (took, wrote, apologized, re-read, answered, asked, signed) and the past perfect progressive "had been doing" to describe activities leading up to writing the letter.
grammarNote.zh: 叙述使用一般过去时（took、wrote、apologized、re-read、answered、asked、signed），并用过去完成进行时 had been doing 描述写信之前持续进行的活动。

steps.en: I took out some paper to write to my friend.
steps.zh: 我拿出一些纸给朋友写信。

steps.en: I wrote the date and a greeting at the top.
steps.zh: 我在上方写了日期和称呼。

steps.en: I apologized for not writing sooner...
steps.zh: 我为没有早点写信而道歉……

steps.en: ...and I wrote about what I'd been doing.
As I wrote, I re-read her last letter to me.
steps.zh: 写信时，我重读了她上一封给我的信。

steps.en: I answered questions she had asked...
steps.zh: 我回答了她问过的问题……

steps.en: ...and I asked her about herself.
Then I wrote a closing...
...and signed the letter.

verbs.zh: 做；（过去完成进行时）一直在做

notes.en: Stationery is paper especially for writing letters.
notes.zh: 信纸是专门用来写信的纸张。

notes.en: When you re-read something, you read it again — not for the first time.
notes.zh: re-read（重读）就是把东西再读一遍——不是第一次读。

notes.en: What I had been doing means what I did during a period of time before I wrote the letter.
notes.zh: “我之前一直在做的事”指我在写信之前一段时间里所做的事。

notes.en: A personal letter is a letter to a friend or relative. It is written differently from a business letter.
notes.zh: 私人信件是写给朋友或亲戚的信，写法与商务信件不同。

notes.en: The greeting in a letter usually starts with "Dear," e.g., "Dear Mom," "Dear Jim," etc.
notes.zh: 信里的称呼通常以“Dear”开头，例如“Dear Mom”“Dear Jim”等。

notes.en: The closing of a letter comes just before your signature.
notes.zh: 信的结尾敬语就在签名之前。

china.en: In China, handwritten personal letters are rare; people use WeChat messages, QQ, or email to stay in touch.
china.zh: 在中国，手写信件很少见，人们用微信、QQ 或电子邮件联系。

china.en: Long-distance communication is nearly free through smartphone apps, so postage stamps are rarely used.
china.zh: 通过手机应用长途通讯几乎免费，邮票很少使用。

china.en: New Year greetings are often sent as WeChat red envelopes or e-cards instead of paper cards.
china.zh: 新年祝福常用微信红包或电子贺卡发送，而非纸质卡片。

grammarNote.en: Sending a package is described as a routine procedure using the simple present tense (I put, I write, I seal, I stand, I weigh, I pay).
grammarNote.zh: 寄包裹作为一种常规流程使用一般现在时叙述（I put、I write、I seal、I stand、I weigh、I pay）。

steps.en: I put a picture in a small box.
steps.zh: 我把一幅画放进小盒子里。

steps.en: I write Grandma's address on the box.
steps.zh: 我在盒子上写奶奶的地址。

steps.en: I seal the box with tape.
I take the box to the express station.
steps.zh: 我把盒子带到快递驿站。

steps.en: I stand in line.
When it's my turn, I give the box to the clerk.
steps.zh: 轮到我时，我把盒子递给工作人员。

steps.en: He asks me where I want to send it...
...and weighs the box.
I pay the fee with my mom's phone.
steps.zh: 我用妈妈的手机扫码付款。

steps.en: He gives me a receipt and a tracking number.
steps.zh: 他给我回执和快递单号。

notes.en: Stand in line — usually without "a" or "the." When you stand in line, you wait for your turn.
notes.zh: stand in line（排队）通常不加 a 或 the，排队就是等待轮到你。

notes.en: An express station (快递驿站) is a small shop where you can send and pick up packages.
notes.zh: express station（快递驿站）是收发包裹的小店。

notes.en: A tracking number lets you follow the package on your phone until it arrives.
notes.zh: 快递单号可以让你在手机上跟踪包裹，直到它送达。

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: I hope Grandma likes the picture!

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.en: Where do you want to send it?

china.en: In China, sending things is mostly done at express stations or by door pickup; stamps and post offices are rare.
china.zh: 在中国，寄东西主要去快递驿站或上门取件，邮票和邮局很少见了。

china.en: People pay the delivery fee by scanning a code, and track the package with the tracking number on the phone.
china.zh: 大家扫码付快递费，再用快递单号在手机上跟踪物流。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes the usual, repeated steps of going to a birthday party: I wrap, I give, someone lights, we sing, he opens, everyone eats.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述参加生日聚会通常的、重复的步骤：I wrap、I give、someone lights、we sing、he opens、everyone eats。

steps.en: Before the party, I wrap a present for my friend...
steps.zh: 聚会前，我给朋友包了一份礼物……

steps.en: ...and sign a card for him.
At the party, I give him the present and the card.
steps.zh: 聚会上，我把礼物和贺卡给他。

steps.en: Someone lights the candles on the birthday cake.
steps.zh: 有人点燃了生日蛋糕上的蜡烛。

steps.en: We all sing "Happy Birthday"...
steps.zh: 我们大家一起唱“生日快乐”……

steps.en: ...and Leo blows out the candles.
He opens his birthday presents...
...and then everyone eats cake and ice cream.

notes.en: A present is a gift for a special occasion (a birthday, Christmas, etc.).
notes.zh: present（礼物）是为特殊场合（生日、圣诞节等）准备的礼品。

notes.en: You wrap a present in wrapping paper.
notes.zh: 你用包装纸把礼物包起来。

notes.en: You open a present by taking off the wrapping paper.
notes.zh: 你撕开包装纸打开礼物。

notes.en: You light a candle by making the wick burn.
notes.zh: 你点燃烛芯使蜡烛燃烧。

notes.en: When you blow out a candle, the fire stops burning.
notes.zh: 当你吹灭蜡烛时，火焰就停止燃烧。

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: Here you go, Leo. Happy birthday.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.en: Hey, I've been wanting this CD. Thanks.
dialogue.zh: 嘿，我一直想要这张 CD。谢谢。

china.en: In China, birthday gifts are often red envelopes (hongbao) with money, or practical items bought online.
china.zh: 在中国，生日礼物常是红包，或网购的实用物品。

china.en: Birthday cakes and singing "Happy Birthday" are popular, and friends also treat the birthday person to a meal.
china.zh: 生日蛋糕和唱“生日快乐”很流行，朋友们也会请客吃饭。

china.en: People often post birthday wishes on WeChat Moments rather than hand-making cards.
china.zh: 人们常在微信朋友圈发生日祝福，而不是手写贺卡。

grammarNote.en: The simple present describes the typical sequence of a dinner party: greets, give, say hello, introduces, shake hands, make small talk, have dinner, say goodnight.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述晚宴的典型流程：greets、give、say hello、introduces、shake hands、make small talk、have dinner、say goodnight。

steps.en: Dan (the host) greets Tom and Jenny (the guests) at the door.
steps.zh: 丹（主人）在门口迎接汤姆和珍妮（客人）。

steps.en: They give him a bottle of wine they brought.
steps.zh: 他们把带来的一瓶酒送给他。

steps.en: Inside, they say hello to some people they know.
steps.zh: 进屋后，他们跟认识的人打招呼。

steps.en: Dan introduces them to some people.
steps.zh: 丹把他们介绍给其他人。

steps.en: They shake hands...
...and make some small talk.
They have their dinner.
At the end of the evening, the guests say goodnight and thank Dan.
steps.zh: 晚会结束时，客人们道晚安并感谢丹。

notes.en: It's polite in America for a guest at an adult party to bring a bottle of wine. It's also polite for a host to say that the gift is unnecessary.
notes.zh: 在美国，成人聚会上客人带一瓶酒是礼貌的；主人说礼物不必客气也是礼貌的。

notes.en: Small talk is talk about some unimportant topic like the weather or sports. You "make small talk" and "make conversation."
notes.zh: small talk 是谈论天气、体育等不重要的话题。说“make small talk”或“make conversation”。

notes.en: The evening is the time from about sundown until about midnight.
notes.zh: evening（傍晚到晚上）指从日落到午夜前后的这段时间。

dialogue.speaker: Dan
dialogue.en: Hi Tom, Jenny. Glad you could come.
dialogue.zh: 嗨，汤姆，珍妮。很高兴你们能来。

dialogue.speaker: Dan
dialogue.en: Thanks, Jenny, but you didn't have to bring anything.
dialogue.zh: 谢谢，珍妮，但你们不用带东西的。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Leo. Kate. Good to see you.
dialogue.zh: 利奥，凯特，见到你们真高兴。

dialogue.speaker: Dan
dialogue.en: Tom, Jenny, I'd like you to meet Sharon Melton and her husband, John.
dialogue.zh: 汤姆，珍妮，来认识一下莎伦·梅尔顿和她丈夫约翰。

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.en: Sure was a hot one today.

dialogue.speaker: Dan
dialogue.en: Glad you could come. Drive safely.
dialogue.zh: 很高兴你们能来。路上小心。

china.en: In China, dinner parties are often held at restaurants rather than at home, and the host usually pays.
china.zh: 在中国，聚餐常在餐厅而不是家里，通常由主人买单。

china.en: Bringing wine is less common; guests may bring fruit, tea, or a small gift instead.
china.zh: 带葡萄酒不太常见；客人可能带水果、茶叶或小礼物。

china.en: Toasting with baijiu and playing drinking games is common at Chinese dinner gatherings.
china.zh: 中式聚餐上劝酒、玩酒桌游戏很常见。

grammarNote.en: The simple past narrates a completed trip to the movies: found, bought, went, tore, gave, watched, saw. Irregular verbs include buy→bought, find→found, give→gave, go→went, see→saw, tear→tore.
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时叙述一次已完成的观影经历：found、bought、went、tore、gave、watched、saw。不规则动词有 buy→bought、find→found、give→gave、go→went、see→saw、tear→tore。

steps.en: We found out where and when the movie was showing.
steps.zh: 我们弄清楚了电影在哪里、什么时候放映。

steps.en: We bought tickets at the box office...
...and some popcorn at the snack counter.
The ticket-taker tore our tickets and gave us back the stubs.
steps.zh: 检票员撕了我们的票，把票根还给我们。

steps.en: We went to our seats.
steps.zh: 我们走到自己的座位上。

steps.en: We watched previews of coming attractions.
steps.zh: 我们看了即将上映电影的预告片。

steps.en: Then we saw the main feature.
At the end, we watched the credits.
steps.zh: 结束时，我们看了片尾字幕。

nouns.zh: 即将上映的影片预告片

notes.en: Coming attractions are movies that will soon be shown.
notes.zh: coming attractions 是即将上映的电影。

notes.en: The movie is showing means "the movie is being shown."
notes.zh: “The movie is showing”意思是“电影正在放映”。

notes.en: The box office is the place where tickets to movies are sold. It can also be called a "ticket window."
notes.zh: box office 是卖电影票的地方，也叫 ticket window。

notes.en: A stub is a small piece. A ticket stub is a piece torn off a ticket.
notes.zh: stub 是一小片东西；票根是从票上撕下来的一小片。

notes.en: If you see a preview, you will see a small part of something you can see completely later.
notes.zh: 看预告片就是先看到以后才能完整看到的东西的一小部分。

notes.en: The main feature is the movie you have come to see.
notes.zh: main feature 就是你专门来看的那部正片。

notes.en: Credits tell who worked on the movie.
notes.zh: credits（片尾字幕）告诉你哪些人参与了这部电影。

china.en: In China, movie tickets are usually bought on phone apps like Maoyan or Taobao, with reserved seats chosen from a seating chart.
china.zh: 在中国，电影票通常在猫眼或淘宝等手机 App 上购买，并通过座位图选座。

china.en: Tickets are scanned at the entrance from the phone screen; paper tickets and stubs are rarely used.
china.zh: 入场时手机扫码检票，纸质票和票根很少使用。

china.en: Snacks at Chinese cinemas often include iced tea, chicken wings, and spicy strips, not just popcorn.
china.zh: 中国影院的零食除了爆米花，还有冰红茶、鸡翅、辣条等。

units.en: Eating at a Fast Food Restaurant

grammarNote.en: This story uses the simple past: Jenny stood, read, ordered, paid, ate, threw... Irregular verbs in this unit: stand→stood, read→read, pay→paid, eat→ate, take→took, throw→threw, get→got.
grammarNote.zh: 这个故事用一般过去时叙述：stood、read、ordered、paid、ate、threw……本单元的不规则动词：stand→stood、read→read、pay→paid、eat→ate、take→took、throw→threw、get→got。

steps.en: Jenny stood in line and read the menu.
steps.zh: 珍妮排着队，看了看菜单。

steps.en: She ordered her food and a drink at the counter.
steps.zh: 她在柜台点了食物和饮料。

steps.en: The clerk put the food on her tray, and Jenny paid her.
steps.zh: 店员把食物放到托盘上，珍妮付了钱。

steps.en: Jenny took some paper napkins and a straw from the dispensers.
steps.zh: 珍妮从取用架拿了纸巾和吸管。

steps.en: She ate her lunch at her table.
steps.zh: 她在自己的桌旁吃了午餐。

steps.en: Other people got their food to go.
steps.zh: 其他人把食物打包带走。

steps.en: When she finished eating, she threw the empty wrappers in the trash.
steps.zh: 吃完后，她把空的包装扔进垃圾桶。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: I'd like one Big Burger, a small order of fries, and a medium cola, please.
dialogue.zh: 我想要一个巨无霸汉堡、一份小薯条和一杯中杯可乐。

notes.en: In a fast-food restaurant, the menu is usually on a big board on the wall.
notes.zh: 快餐店的菜单通常写在一块很大的墙面上。

notes.en: “For here” means you eat in the restaurant. “To go” means you eat outside. You can also say “to take away” or “to take out”.
notes.zh: For here 表示在店里吃（堂食）；to go 表示带走吃，也可以说 to take away 或 to take out（打包）。

notes.en: Wrappers are the paper or boxes around the food to keep it fresh.
notes.zh: wrapper（包装）是包在食物外面的纸或盒子，用来保鲜。

china.en: In China, you can also pay by scanning a QR code with WeChat Pay or Alipay.
china.zh: 在中国快餐店，还可以用微信支付或支付宝扫码付款：scan the QR code（扫码）。

china.en: “For here or to go?” is just like “堂食还是打包？” in Chinese fast-food restaurants.
china.zh: For here or to go? 就相当于中国快餐店的“堂食还是打包？”

china.en: Many people in China order fast food on their phones and get it delivered.
china.zh: 中国很多人用手机 App 点快餐外卖（order food delivery），在家就能吃。也可以说 order food on the app。

grammarNote.en: We use the simple present to talk about what we do every day. Examples: Jenny puts on her schoolbag. She walks to the school gate. Her friend waves to her. Time words: every morning, every day, always, usually.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时用来描述每天都会做的事。例句：Jenny puts on her schoolbag.（珍妮背上书包。）She walks to the school gate.（她走到学校门口。）常搭配时间词：every morning 每天早上、every day 每天、always 总是、usually 通常。

steps.en: Jenny puts on her schoolbag.
She goes downstairs with her mom.
They walk to the school gate.
Jenny says goodbye to her mom.
She walks into the school.
Her friend waves to her.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Bye, Mom! Have a good day!
dialogue.zh: 再见，妈妈！祝你今天愉快！

dialogue.speaker: Mom
dialogue.en: Bye, sweetie! Be good at school.
dialogue.zh: 再见，宝贝！在学校要乖哦。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Good morning! Let's go to class.
dialogue.zh: 早上好！我们一起去上课吧。

notes.en: “Have a good day!” is a friendly way to say goodbye in the morning.
notes.zh: Have a good day!（祝你今天愉快！）是早上告别时的友好说法。

notes.en: A parent calls a child “sweetie” to show love.
notes.zh: 爸爸妈妈会叫孩子 sweetie（宝贝）表示疼爱。

notes.en: “Let's” is short for “let us”. It means “we should do this together”.
notes.zh: Let's 是 let us 的缩写，表示“我们一起做某事吧”。

china.en: In Chinese cities, many parents walk or ride an e-bike with their child to the school gate, and parents usually stop outside the gate.
china.zh: 在中国城市，很多家长走路或骑电动车送孩子到校门口，家长一般不进校。

china.en: Chinese students say goodbye at the gate and walk into school by themselves, just like Jenny.
china.zh: 中国学生在校门口和家长道别后自己走进学校，就像珍妮一样。

china.en: “Have a good day!” is like saying “好好学习，再见！” at the school gate.
china.zh: Have a good day! 就像在校门口说“好好学习，再见！”

grammarNote.en: We use the imperative to give instructions. The verb comes first, without “you”. Examples: Open your books. Raise your hand. Line up, please. We can add “please” to be polite: Open your books, please.
grammarNote.zh: 祈使句用来发出指令，动词开头、不加主语 you。例句：Open your books.（打开课本。）Raise your hand.（举手。）Line up, please.（请排队。）加 please 更有礼貌。

steps.en: The bell rings.
Jenny sits at her desk.
The teacher says, “Open your books.”
Jenny raises her hand.
She writes in her notebook.
The bell rings again.
The children line up.
They play on the playground.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Good morning, class. Open your books, please.
dialogue.zh: 同学们早上好。请打开课本。

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.en: The bell is ringing! Let's go out to play.

notes.en: “May I…?” is a polite way to ask for permission. It is more polite than “Can I…?”.
notes.zh: May I…?（我可以……吗？）是比 Can I…? 更礼貌的请求许可的说法。

notes.en: “Line up” means to stand one behind another to make a line.
notes.zh: line up（排队）指一个接一个站成一条队。

notes.en: Recess is the short break between classes, when children can play.
notes.zh: recess（课间）是两节课之间的短休息时间，孩子们可以玩。

china.en: In Chinese primary schools, students stand up and say hello to the teacher when the bell rings.
china.zh: 中国小学上课铃响后，学生起立向老师问好。

china.en: Chinese students raise their hand and say “May I ask a question?” before speaking in class.
china.zh: 中国学生在课堂上先举手，说“May I ask a question?”（我可以问个问题吗？）再发言。

china.en: During the ten-minute recess, children play in the hallway or on the playground.
china.zh: 课间十分钟，孩子们在走廊或操场上玩。

grammarNote.en: We use the simple present to talk about things we do and happen every time. Examples: Jenny makes a shopping list. She gets a shopping cart. Mom picks out some apples. The verbs stay in the base form for “I, you, we, they”, and add -s for “he, she, it”: Mom picks out some apples.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述经常做的事。例句：Jenny makes a shopping list.（珍妮列购物清单。）第三人称单数（he/she/it）动词要加 -s：Mom picks out some apples.（妈妈挑了一些苹果。）

steps.en: Jenny makes a shopping list with her mom.
steps.zh: 珍妮和妈妈一起列购物清单。

steps.en: She gets a shopping cart.
Mom picks out some apples.
Jenny puts the apples in the cart.
steps.zh: 珍妮把苹果放进购物车。

steps.en: They weigh the fruit.
They pay at the counter.
Jenny helps carry the bags home.
steps.zh: 珍妮帮忙把袋子拎回家。

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Mom, can I push the cart?
dialogue.zh: 妈妈，我可以推购物车吗？

notes.en: “Can I…?” is used to ask for permission: Can I push the cart? — Yes, you can.
notes.zh: Can I…?（我可以……吗？）用来请求许可：Can I push the cart?——Yes, you can.（可以。）

notes.en: “Let's get some fruit” means “we should buy some fruit together”.
notes.zh: Let's get some fruit（我们买点水果吧）表示“我们一起去买”。

notes.en: In many supermarkets, fruit and vegetables are weighed before paying.
notes.zh: 很多超市的水果蔬菜要先称重再付款。

china.en: In Chinese supermarkets, fresh fruit is weighed at a scale station and a price tag is printed before you go to the counter.
china.zh: 中国超市的生鲜水果要在称重台称重并贴价格标签，再去收银台付款。

china.en: People in China usually pay by scanning a QR code with WeChat Pay or Alipay.
china.zh: 中国人在超市通常用微信或支付宝扫码付款（scan the QR code）。

china.en: Many supermarkets charge a little for plastic bags, so people bring their own shopping bags.
china.zh: 很多中国超市塑料袋收费，所以大家会自己带购物袋（环保袋）。

grammarNote.en: We use the simple present for things we do again and again. Examples: Jenny climbs up the ladder. She goes down the slide. They play on the seesaw. Remember: he / she / it verbs add -s: She goes down the slide.
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述反复做的事。例句：Jenny climbs up the ladder.（珍妮爬上梯子。）She goes down the slide.（她滑下滑梯。）第三人称单数动词加 -s：She goes down the slide. 注意 go 变成 goes。

steps.en: Jenny goes to the playground with her friend.
steps.zh: 珍妮和朋友一起去游乐场。

steps.en: She climbs up the ladder.
She goes down the slide.
They play on the seesaw.
Jenny swings on the swing.
Her friend pushes her.
They go home before dark.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Can I play on the swing, too?

notes.en: “My turn!” means it is my chance to play. “Your turn!” means it is your chance.
notes.zh: My turn!（该我了！）表示轮到我玩；Your turn!（该你了！）表示轮到你。

notes.en: A seesaw goes up and down when two children sit on the two ends.
notes.zh: seesaw（跷跷板）是两人分坐两端、一起一落的玩具。

notes.en: “Before dark” means before the sky gets dark at night.
notes.zh: before dark（天黑前）指夜晚天空变暗之前。

china.en: In China, children often play at the playground in a park or near their apartment building after school.
china.zh: 在中国，孩子放学后常在公园或小区里的儿童游乐区玩。

china.en: Children wait in line and take turns on the slide and the swing.
china.zh: 中国孩子玩滑梯、秋千要排队轮流（take turns），先来后到。

china.en: Parents usually call their children home before dark.
china.zh: 天黑前家长一般会叫孩子回家。

grammarNote.en: We use the imperative to tell someone what to do. The verb comes first: Put your toys away. Pick up the blocks. Put the blocks in the box. To be polite, we can say “please”: Put your toys away, please.
grammarNote.zh: 祈使句用来告诉别人做什么，动词开头：Put your toys away.（把玩具收好。）Pick up the blocks.（捡起积木。）加 please 更礼貌：Put your toys away, please.

steps.en: Mom says, “Put your toys away.”
Jenny picks up the blocks.
She puts the blocks in the box.
She puts the teddy bear on the shelf.
steps.zh: 她把泰迪熊放到架子上。

steps.en: She puts the picture books on the desk.
The room is clean now.
Mom says, “Good job!”

notes.en: “Put away” means to put things back in their proper place.
notes.zh: put away（收好）指把东西放回该放的地方。

notes.en: “Good job!” is what we say to praise a child for doing something well.
notes.zh: Good job!（真棒！）是孩子做得好时用来表扬的话。

notes.en: “All done!” means everything is finished.
notes.zh: All done!（都做好了！）表示全部完成。

china.en: Chinese parents often ask children to tidy up their toys before dinner or before bed.
china.zh: 中国家长常让孩子在吃饭前或睡觉前把玩具收好。

china.en: Many Chinese families keep toys in storage boxes or on a toy shelf in the children's room.
china.zh: 很多中国家庭把玩具收在收纳箱或儿童房的玩具架上。

china.en: Tidying up toys is usually the first chore a Chinese child learns at home.
china.zh: 收玩具通常是中国孩子在家学会的第一件家务。

grammarNote.en: We use the simple present to describe a bedtime routine. Examples: Jenny puts on her pajamas. She sits on the bed. Mom reads her a story. Notice the double object: reads her a story (her = Jenny, a story = the thing read).
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时描述睡前的固定流程。例句：Jenny puts on her pajamas.（珍妮穿上睡衣。）Mom reads her a story.（妈妈给她读故事。）注意双宾语结构 reads her a story：her 指珍妮，a story 是读的内容。

steps.en: Jenny puts on her pajamas.
She sits on the bed.
Mom reads her a story.
Jenny hugs her teddy bear.
Mom turns off the light.
Jenny says, “Goodnight, Mom.”
Mom says, “Sweet dreams.”

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Mom, read me a story, please.
dialogue.zh: 妈妈，请给我读个故事吧。

dialogue.speaker: Mom
dialogue.en: OK. Which story do you want?

notes.en: “Read me a story” = “read a story to me”. The person comes first: read me a story.
notes.zh: Read me a story 等于 read a story to me（给我读个故事），人放在前面。

notes.en: “Sweet dreams” is what parents say to children at night. It means “sleep well and dream nice dreams”.
notes.zh: Sweet dreams（做个好梦）是家长晚上对孩子说的祝福语。

notes.en: “Goodnight” is said when someone is going to bed at night.
notes.zh: Goodnight（晚安）是晚上睡觉前说的话。

china.en: Reading picture books before bed is a common parenting activity in Chinese families.
china.zh: 睡前读绘本是中国家庭常见的亲子活动。

china.en: Chinese children often hug a soft toy or a favorite blanket when they sleep.
china.zh: 中国孩子睡觉时常抱着玩偶或喜欢的毯子。

china.en: Saying “晚安，妈妈” and “做个好梦” is just like Jenny's goodnight in the unit.
china.zh: “晚安，妈妈”“做个好梦”正是本单元里珍妮和妈妈的对话。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes Jenny's usual Saturday routine: goes, sits, takes out, draws, shows, practices. / 一般现在时描述 Jenny 每周六的兴趣班常规活动：goes、sits、takes out、draws、shows、practices。
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时

steps.en: Jenny goes to an art class on Saturday.
steps.zh: 珍妮每周六去上美术课。

steps.en: She sits at the table and takes out her crayons.
She draws a picture of her family.
She shows the picture to her teacher.
The teacher says, "Good job! What a nice drawing!"
steps.zh: 老师说：“画得真好！多漂亮的画呀！”

steps.en: After class, Mom picks her up.
Jenny says, "I like drawing! Can I practice more?"
steps.zh: 珍妮说：“我喜欢画画！我能多练习一会儿吗？”

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Good job! What a nice drawing!
dialogue.zh: 画得真好！多漂亮的画呀！

notes.en: "Good job!" is what we say to praise someone for doing well.
notes.zh: Good job!（干得好！）是我们表扬别人做得好时说的话。

notes.en: "Can I practice more?" is a polite way to ask permission.
notes.zh: Can I practice more?（我能多练一会儿吗？）是礼貌地请求允许。

notes.en: Many Chinese children take after-school classes like art, piano, dance or calligraphy on weekends.
notes.zh: 很多中国孩子周末上美术、钢琴、舞蹈或书法等兴趣班。

china.en: After-school classes are very common for Chinese children; art, piano, dance and calligraphy are popular choices.
china.zh: 中国孩子上兴趣班非常普遍，美术、钢琴、舞蹈、书法都是热门选择。

china.en: Parents often pick children up after class and ask "What did you learn today?"
china.zh: 家长常在下课后接孩子，并问“今天学了什么？”。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense tells the story of Jenny's birthday: made, blew out, cut, sang, opened, said, had. Irregular verbs: make→made, blow→blew, cut→cut, sing→sang, open→opened. / 一般过去时讲述 Jenny 过生日的过程：made、blew out、cut、sang、opened、said、had。不规则动词：make→made、blow→blew、cut→cut、sing→sang。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: It was Jenny's birthday.
Mom made a cake for her.
steps.zh: 妈妈给她做了一个蛋糕。

steps.en: Jenny made a wish and blew out the candles.
steps.zh: 珍妮许了愿，吹灭了蜡烛。

steps.en: Her friends sang "Happy Birthday."
steps.zh: 朋友们唱了《生日快乐》歌。

steps.en: She cut the cake.
She opened the presents and said thank you.
Everyone had a good time.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Thank you! I made a wish.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: A toy panda! Thank you so much!
dialogue.zh: 一只玩具熊猫！太谢谢你了！

notes.en: Make a wish, then blow out the candles — a birthday tradition.
notes.zh: 许愿、吹蜡烛是过生日的传统环节。

notes.en: "This is for you." is what you say when you give someone a present.
notes.zh: 送礼物时说 This is for you.（这是送给你的）。

notes.en: "Thank you so much!" is a warmer way to say thank you.
notes.zh: Thank you so much! 是更热情的道谢方式。

china.en: Chinese children celebrate birthdays with a cake, candles, a wish and presents, just like Jenny.
china.zh: 中国孩子过生日也有蛋糕、蜡烛、许愿和礼物，和珍妮一样。

china.en: Parents often take photos and share them on WeChat Moments.
china.zh: 家长常会拍照并分享到微信朋友圈。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense narrates the visit to the doctor: went, waited, measured, looked, said, got, hurt. Irregular verbs: go→went, say→said, get→got. / 一般过去时讲述看医生的一次经历：went、waited、measured、looked、said、got、hurt。不规则动词：go→went、say→said、get→got。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: Jenny went to the doctor with her mom.
They waited in the waiting room.
The nurse measured her height and weight.
steps.zh: 护士给她量了身高和体重。

steps.en: The doctor looked in her ears and throat.
steps.zh: 医生看了看她的耳朵和喉咙。

steps.en: He said, "Open your mouth and say 'Ah.'"
Jenny got a small shot. It hurt a little.
steps.zh: 珍妮打了一针，有一点疼。

steps.en: Mom said, "You'll be fine." And the doctor gave her a sticker.
steps.zh: 妈妈说：“会没事的。”医生还给了她一张贴纸。

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.en: Great job! Here's a sticker for you.

notes.en: "Open your mouth and say 'Ah'" is what the doctor says to check your throat.
notes.zh: “张开嘴说啊”是医生检查喉咙时说的话。

notes.en: A shot (打针) hurts a little, but it keeps you healthy.
notes.zh: 打针会有一点疼，但它能让你保持健康。

notes.en: The doctor's office measures your height and weight to see how you grow.
notes.zh: 医生那里量身高体重，是为了看你的成长情况。

china.en: In China, children visit the hospital or clinic for check-ups and vaccines; parents register and take a number first.
china.zh: 在中国，孩子去医院或诊所做体检、打疫苗，家长先挂号取号。

china.en: Pediatricians often comfort children with stickers or small gifts after a shot.
china.zh: 儿科医生常在打针后用贴纸或小礼物安抚孩子。

grammarNote.en: The simple present tense describes the usual way Jenny talks with her friend: video-calls, answers, waves, shows, talks, hangs up. / 一般现在时描述珍妮和同学视频通话的常规过程：video-calls、answers、waves、shows、talks、hangs up。
grammarNote.zh: 一般现在时

steps.en: Jenny video-calls her classmate Kate.
steps.zh: 珍妮给同学凯特打视频电话。

steps.en: Kate answers the video call.
They wave and say hi.
Jenny shows Kate her drawing.
Kate says, "Wow! I like your drawing."
steps.zh: 凯特说：“哇！我喜欢你的画。”

steps.en: They talk about school.
At the end, they say goodbye and hang up.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Look what I made! It's a drawing of our school.
dialogue.zh: 看我画了什么！是我们学校。

dialogue.speaker: Kate
dialogue.en: Wow! I like it. It's beautiful.

notes.en: Video-call is a verb here: to talk with someone on a screen.
notes.zh: video-call 在这里是动词：通过屏幕和人通话。

notes.en: "Look what I made!" is how you show something you made with pride.
notes.zh: Look what I made!（看我做的！）是自豪地展示自己作品的说法。

notes.en: In China, kids often video-call grandparents and classmates on WeChat.
notes.zh: 在中国，孩子常用微信和爷爷奶奶、同学视频通话。

china.en: WeChat video calls are the most common way for Chinese kids to stay in touch with family and classmates.
china.zh: 微信视频通话是中国孩子和家人、同学保持联系最常见的方式。

china.en: Children love to show their drawings, toys or homework on a video call.
china.zh: 孩子们喜欢在视频里展示自己的画、玩具或作业。

grammarNote.en: The simple past tense tells what happened after dinner: went, played, counted, looked for, jumped, kicked, got dark, called. Irregular verbs: go→went, get→got. / 一般过去时讲述晚饭后在楼下玩耍的经过：went、played、counted、looked for、jumped、kicked、got dark、called。不规则动词：go→went、get→got。
grammarNote.zh: 一般过去时

steps.en: After dinner, Jenny went downstairs to play.
Her friends were in the yard.
They played hide-and-seek.
Jenny counted to ten and looked for her friends.
steps.zh: 珍妮数到十，然后去找朋友们。

steps.en: Then they jumped rope together.
Tom kicked a ball to Jenny.
When it got dark, Mom called her home.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Mom, can I go out and play?

dialogue.speaker: Mom
dialogue.en: Yes, but come home before dark.

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: Ready or not, here I come!

dialogue.speaker: Jenny
dialogue.en: OK, Mom. Can I play a little longer?
dialogue.zh: 好的，妈妈。我能再玩一会儿吗？

notes.en: In hide-and-seek, one child counts, the others hide, then the first child looks for them.
notes.zh: 捉迷藏时，一个孩子数数，其他人藏起来，然后他去找。

notes.en: "Ready or not, here I come!" is what the seeker says after counting.
notes.zh: “准备好了没？我来找啦！”是数完数后去找人时说的话。

notes.en: Playing outside is fun, but come home before dark.
notes.zh: 在外面玩很开心，但要天黑前回家。

china.en: After dinner, Chinese children often play in the yard or open space of the housing community with friends.
china.zh: 晚饭后，中国孩子常和伙伴在小区院子里或楼下空地上玩。

china.en: Parents call kids home when it gets dark; "come home before dark" is a common family rule.
china.zh: 天黑了家长会喊孩子回家，“天黑前回家”是常见的家规。
